title: Submarine Cable Repair Capacities - Works
descriptionByte:
Expected Impact:

The expected benefits of the supported project:

  • Provide quick response to emergency situations identified by the relevant Regional Cable Hub or other entity declaring the emergency situation (Key Performance Indicator).

  • Provide quick average estimated time-to-repair for cable systems in the targeted EU sea basins with at least one landing point in an EU territory (Key Performance Indicator).

  • Increase operational repair capacity in the main European sea basins (Key Performance Indicator).

  • Strengthen the resilience of cable systems in the main European sea basins.

  • Ensure digital sovereignty and strategic autonomy of the EU in the main European sea basins.

Objective:

This call aims to enhance emergency response capacities and the resilience of backbone networks’ infrastructures by supporting the development and deployment of adaptable repair modules for swift emergency repair operations, enabling quick response to incidents that could severely impact the Union or its Member States.

The goal of the EU is to fund modules covering the main sea basins of the Union, the objective being to develop adaptable repair modules that can be deployed on existing vessels, as well as the necessary related operational capabilities.

The modules are expected to be rapidly operational in order to re-establish the service of submarine cables (through repair or substitution) in emergency situations, i.e. where the cut or the failure of the cable can cause a severe damage to one or more Member States, and the service disruption cannot be fixed timely by commercial services. Applicants will have to work in coordination with the authorities declaring the emergency situation, which are expected to be the future Regional Cable Hubs4.

The modules would be hosted in ports or shipyards with the capacity to install them on board of ships within a maximum of 3 days from the arrival of the vessel at the port/shipyard, following a request by the Regional Surveillance Hub envisaged in the Action Plan on Cable Security.

Scope:

This call funds modular equipment for the repair of telecom submarine cables, and targets public entities with an emergency response mandate such as entities active in the civil protection, national emergency response agencies, coastguards and military navies. Each Member State will confirm the nature of the applicant in the mandatory Letter of Support.

Beneficiaries can subcontract the activities covered by this call for proposals as well as the operation of the modules for repair intervention to third parties, including publicly or privately owned entities without an emergency response mandate. However, the modules can only be used to respond to emergency situations declared by the competent authority.

The pre-configured vessels are flat deck vessels that should be able to receive the modules with minor adaptation and operational preparation, and without regulatory or technical barriers. Therefore, the proposals should demonstrate the adaptability, portability and scalability of the solution put forward.

To make sure that the modular equipment will be ready for intervention, applicants should identify at least three vessels that are or will be pre-configured for receiving the modules. Costs for pre-configuration of the vessels can be included in the proposal provided that they comply with the eligibility conditions of this call.

Applicants should explain in detail in their proposal how the vessels are already pre-configured or how they plan to carry out the above-mentioned pre-configuration, and how many pre-configured vessels will be made available. For vessels owned by third parties, applicants should provide details on lease or service level agreement guaranteeing the availability of these vessels to receive the modules over their economic lifespan (at least 10 years).

Proposals should also demonstrate solid implementation plans, including the definition of compatible specifications for the vessels and the different types of modules, project’s phasing (design, production-level deployment, operation), governance, allocation policies, financial aspects, as well as the rationale for the choice of the storage and installation locations. To this purpose, it is crucial that the proposals clearly demonstrate effective, reliable and efficient coordination with all relevant stakeholders, especially the entity declaring the emergency situation which is expected to be the future Regional Cable Hubs. The solidity of the plan will be taken into account when assessing the maturity of the proposal.

Proposals should demonstrate how they contribute to CPEI Area 8 (“Multipurpose vessel(s) and modular equipment stock”) from the CPEI list published in February 2026, and in particular to one or more of the CPEI criteria b, c, d and e of Point 26, and CPEI criteria a, b and c of Point 27 of Commission Recommendation (EU) 2024/779.

Proposals must provide repair modules to increase repair capacity for all subsea cable systems, serving EU Member States in the main European sea basins following the current repair agreements when relevant.

Please consult the call document for more information on the scope, including digital security requirements.

results.summary: Experience sharing grants
results.content: Experience sharing grants

beneficiaryAdministration:
The objective of the Call for thematic grants is to support experience sharing between CSOs that work on behalf of groups at risk of discrimination, unequal treatment, hate speech or hate crime, or that carry out watchdog/monitoring/advocacy activities in support of respect for the rule of law, or that aim to gain experience in these areas within the project.

Experience sharing grants are meant to enable peer learning between two CSOs (Applicant and Partner) of different levels of experience regarding human rights and/or rule of law activities, organisational development, team building, etc. They are intended to encourage CSOs to share skills and solutions.

Total budget for the call: PLN 300 000 approx. EUR 69 460)

Minimum/maximum grant amount: PLN 10 000-20 000 (approx. EUR 2 315-4 600)

In order to be eligible, Applicants must:

- Be established in Poland.

- Be non-profit making and a civil society organisation.

- Respect EU values as laid down in Art.2 of the Treaty on European Union and the EU Charter of fundamental rights.

- Have eligible legal form: foundations, associations registered in the National Court Register, church legal persons registered in the National Court Register, rural housewives’ circles, so called ordinary associations

- Have been registered at least 12 months before submitting the application.

I order to be eligible Partners must:

- Be established in Poland.

- Be non-profit making and a civil society organisation.

- Respect EU values as laid down in Art.2 of the Treaty on European Union and the EU Charter of fundamental rights.

- Have eligible legal form: foundations, associations registered in the National Court Register, church legal persons registered in the National Court Register, rural housewives’ circles, so called ordinary associations.

Only activities taking place in an EU Member State are eligible.

Submitted proposals will be evaluated in an open-end (rolling) call. Grants will be awarded a maximum of four times (until the allocation is exhausted), according to the following schedule:

- until December 19, 2025,

- until April 30, 2026,

- until September 4, 2026,

- until December 18, 2026.

Eligible types of project activities:

• study visits;

• joint workshops;

• job shadowing;

• traineeships;

• exchange of experts between Applicant and Partner;

• joint initiatives testing new working methods. Organisations cannot conduct religious worship as part of the project, and funded activities must not directly or indirectly promote religious doctrine, mission or appeal to a particular faith.

Further information, including a detailed description of the call procedure, can be found on the Equal Rights Programme website: https://programrownychpraw.batory.org.pl/.

results.summary: ReAction – Rapid Response Grants
results.content: ReAction – Rapid Response Grants

beneficiaryAdministration:
Bulgarian Fund for Women (BFW) launches ReAction – Rapid Response Grants with a total budget of €300,000. The call is open-ended: civil society organisations (CSOs) in Bulgaria may apply at any time until March 2028 or until funds are fully allocated.


Who can apply:

• Public benefit associations or foundations registered in Bulgaria, independent of political, state, religious, or commercial interests.

• Priority is given to small, grassroots, rural and underfunded CSOs, including those representing women, LGBTIQ+ people, minorities, refugees, or working on climate justice.


What is funded:

Rapid response grants of up to €10,000 (max. 12 months) to address:

• Crisis situations and attacks on organisations;

• Urgent advocacy or mobilisation opportunities;

• Holistic security for activists;

• Organisational transition in emergencies;

• Emergency support for marginalised communities.


Application process:

• Applications are submitted online via BFW’s Salesforce platform: Apply here.

• Information about the process can be found here.


Evaluation criteria:

Applications will be assessed on:

• Relevance to programme objectives;

• Urgency and need for immediate action;

• Realism and feasibility of proposed response;

• Contribution to resilience, equality, and EU values;

• Leadership and participation of affected groups.

results.summary: Call for proposal for support to Slovenian and Croatian SCOs to “Go out and vote!” campaigns
results.content: Call for proposal for support to Slovenian and Croatian SCOs to “Go out and vote!” campaigns

beneficiaryAdministration:
Purpose of the call: to provide support to Go out and vote! Campaigns that motivate people to vote for defence of EU values (in Slovenia and Croatia)

Expected results (apply to both countries):

-strengthened civil society watchdog/advocacy role (Increased involvement of CSOs in monitoring of political promises; increased number of CSOs mobilizing citizens in civic activities; increased number of CSOs engaged in civic education; increased number of monitoring tools)

-Increased promotion and public awareness of EU rights and values (increased number of awareness raising actions/campaigns)

Increased civic engagement in environmental protection/climate change (support to innovative methods for the protection of the environment; support for the awareness raising actions/campaigns.)

Submission and evaluation process (apply to both countries):

The call is an open-end call for proposals which will remain open until the budget is exhausted, or until 01/01/2028 at the latest. Applications with the required attachments must be submitted exclusively in electronic form to the designated email address: Croatia – akcije.cerv@zaklada-slagalica.hr; Slovenia - akcije.cerv2@cnvos.si. These email addresses are intended solely for the submission of applications for this Call and will not be monitored before the beginning of the application acceptance date. Applications submitted sooner or in any other way (e.g., by fax, regular mail, etc.) or sent to another email address will be rejected.

Applications must be delivered to the specified email address no sooner than November 5, 2025. Applications delivered to the specified email address before this date will be rejected. The date and time of email delivery with the completed application and all required attachments are those recorded on the server of CNVOS/Community Foundation Slagalica.

After submitting application, applicants will receive an automatic response to the email address from which the application was sent. If such a response does not arrive in the applicant's email inbox or spam folder within two (2) hours after sending the application, applicants may contact CNVOS or CFS during the publicised office hours for check of the application status.

  1. A complete application includes:

● A fully completed application form (Word),

● A fully completed financial plan (Excel),

● A completed form with applicant and project details (Excel),

● A scanned, signed, and stamped Applicant's Statement declaring they accept the conditions of the call, including the compliance with the EU values (in .pdf format),

● A scanned, signed (and stamped) Partner's Statement declaring they accept the conditions of the call, including the compliance with the EU values (in case of partnership) (in .pdf format),

● A scanned valid statute or founding act of the applicant, if the document is not available in a publicly accessible national electronic registry (in .pdf format),

● A scanned valid founding act or statute of the partner, if the document is not available in a publicly accessible national electronic registry (in .pdf format).

Applicants will be notified on the result of their application no later than 14 days after their submission. All applications received shall be assessed according to the selection criteria published in the call. Applicants can submit new application any time after the rejection of the previous one. At the same time, an applicant can have only one on-going ”go out and vote” action.

Evaluation process (apply to both countries):

Administrative check of administrative and eligibility criteria (consortium staff, 4 eyes rule) (see the criteria in the Call document). If certain parts of the project application are missing and can be supplemented (documents or information), applicants will have 5 working days from the date of notification to submit the required supplements. The notification requesting the supplement will be sent to the email address provided by the applicant in the application form (the email address of the contact person).

Applicants whose applications are rejected due to non-compliance with administrative and eligibility criteria will have 8 working days from the date of notification to submit an appeal against the eligibility decision. Appeals will be reviewed by the Complaints Committee, and the Committee’s decision is final. Appeals should be sent to the designated email address for Slovenia/Croatia.

Evaluation of Application Quality (apply to both countries):

Each application that meets the administrative and eligibility criteria will be reviewed and assessed by collective decision-making of the evaluation commission, consisting of 5 members – 3 representatives of the consortium, 2 external experts (1 from Slovenia and 1 from Croatia). As the call will take place on a rolling basis according to a “first come – first serve” principle, there will be no scoring, only YES/NO decisions on each of the criteria (with argumentation). Only projects with all criteria assessed with YES will be supported (see the criteria in the Call document).

Rejected applications can be re-submitted any time, until all funds are exhausted or until 01/01/2028 at the latest.

Due diligence: all proposals that are confirmed by the evaluation committee will be checked on the respect of respect of EU values and double funding.

These email addresses are intended solely for the submission of applications for this Call and will not be monitored before the beginning of the application acceptance date. Applications submitted sooner or in any other way (e.g., by fax, regular mail, etc.) or sent to another email address will be rejected.

Applications must be delivered to the specified email address no sooner than November 5, 2025. Applications delivered to the specified email address before this date will be rejected. The date and time of email delivery with the completed application and all required attachments are those recorded on the server of CNVOS/Community Foundation Slagalica.

After submitting application, applicants will receive an automatic response to the email address from which the application was sent. If such a response does not arrive in the applicant's email inbox or spam folder within two (2) hours after sending the application, applicants may contact CNVOS or CFS during the publicised office hours for check of the application status.

  1. A complete application includes:

● A fully completed application form (Word),

● A fully completed financial plan (Excel),

● A completed form with applicant and project details (Excel),

● A scanned, signed, and stamped Applicant's Statement declaring they accept the conditions of the call, including the compliance with the EU values (in .pdf format),

● A scanned, signed (and stamped) Partner's Statement declaring they accept the conditions of the call, including the compliance with the EU values (in case of partnership) (in .pdf format),

● A scanned valid statute or founding act of the applicant, if the document is not available in a publicly accessible national electronic registry (in .pdf format),

● A scanned valid founding act or statute of the partner, if the document is not available in a publicly accessible national electronic registry (in .pdf format).

Applicants will be notified on the result of their application no later than 14 days after their submission. All applications received shall be assessed according to the selection criteria published in the call. Applicants can submit new application any time after the rejection of the previous one. At the same time, an applicant can have only one on-going ”go out and vote” action.

Evaluation process (apply to both countries):

Administrative check of administrative and eligibility criteria (consortium staff, 4 eyes rule) (see the criteria in the Call document). If certain parts of the project application are missing and can be supplemented (documents or information), applicants will have 5 working days from the date of notification to submit the required supplements. The notification requesting the supplement will be sent to the email address provided by the applicant in the application form (the email address of the contact person).

Applicants whose applications are rejected due to non-compliance with administrative and eligibility criteria will have 8 working days from the date of notification to submit an appeal against the eligibility decision. Appeals will be reviewed by the Complaints Committee, and the Committee’s decision is final. Appeals should be sent to the designated email address for Slovenia/Croatia.

Evaluation of Application Quality (apply to both countries):

Each application that meets the administrative and eligibility criteria will be reviewed and assessed by collective decision-making of the evaluation commission, consisting of 5 members – 3 representatives of the consortium, 2 external experts (1 from Slovenia and 1 from Croatia). As the call will take place on a rolling basis according to a “first come – first serve” principle, there will be no scoring, only YES/NO decisions on each of the criteria (with argumentation). Only projects with all criteria assessed with YES will be supported (see the criteria in the Call document).

Rejected applications can be re-submitted any time, until all funds are exhausted or until 01/01/2028 at the latest.

Due diligence: all proposals that are confirmed by the evaluation committee will be checked on the respect of respect of EU values and double funding.

results.summary: A running call No. 5 for bilateral cooperation project proposals
results.content: A running call No. 5 for bilateral cooperation project proposals

beneficiaryAdministration:
The objective of the call is to establish, develop, and/or improve cooperation between Lithuanian NGOs and advocacy-focused civil society organisations in other EU member states, strengthen organisational capacities, and promote collaboration in the field of advocacy, while upholding EU values. Expected impact includes new and strengthened cross-border partnerships, enhanced advocacy skills, increased mutual learning, and improved public understanding of EU values, including equality and the rights of persons belonging to minorities.

Applications can e submitted in a single-stage procedure at any time starting on the date of call publication until January 31, 2027. All proposals first undergo administrative eligibility checks carried out by the Open Lithuania Foundation (OLF). Eligible applications are then assessed by two independent experts according to predefined quality criteria; if their scores differ by more than 30 points, a third expert is appointed. Following expert assessments, the two closest-scoring experts agree on a consolidated evaluation. The Selection Committee reviews the expert conclusions, may propose budgets adjustments, and approves the list of projects recommended for funding. Applications that fail to reach the minimum required scores or are not in compliance with EU values are excluded from further consideration.

A total of 20 projects will be awarded grants of up to EUR 5,000 each within the maximum threshold allowed for financial support to third parties. Projects may last up to 6 months and will receive lump-sum funding paid in two instalments: 80% upon signing the grant agreement and 20% after the approval of final project reports.

Eligibility requirements for applicants:

  1. The applicant is a legal entity registered in the Republic of Lithuania for at least one year prior to the announcement of the rolling call, i.e., no later than 16 December 2024.
  2. The applicant carries out activities in Lithuania.
  3. The applicant is an NGO established and operating in the Republic of Lithuania that meets the following definition “A non-profit voluntary organisation established as a legal entity, having a non-commercial purpose, independent of local, regional, and central government, public entities, political parties, and commercial organisations.” Religious institutions, trade unions, and political parties are not considered NGOs (definition in line with Article 2.3 of the Law on the Development of Non-Governmental Organizations).
  4. The applicant’s activities do not conflict with EU values and actively contribute (or seek to contribute) to the promotion of EU values.
  5. The applicant has submitted mandatory financial and annual activity reports to the National Center of Registers for the last two years (2023 and 2024), or financial and annual activity reports from the start of its activities if it has been operating for less than three years. Applicants applying after 1 June 2026 must have submitted mandatory financial and annual activity reports for 2024 and 2025.
  6. The Open Lithuania Foundation is not a shareholder of the applicant.
  7. NGOs already participating in the VERTA! Programme (Phase II, 2025–2027) are eligible only if the total cumulative budget of all their applications under the programme, including the amount requested in this call, does not exceed EUR 60,000.
  8. The applicant has not implemented any other bilateral cooperation project under the VERTA! Programme financed from the funds of this call.

Eligibility requirements for partners:

  1. The partner must be a non-governmental organization established and operating as a legal entity in one of the European Union Member States, excluding Lithuania;
  2. The partner conducts advocacy activities in the field of EU values and has at least two years of advocacy experience;
  3. Prior to submitting the application, the applicant and the partner have concluded and signed a letter of intent to cooperate or another type of partnership agreement defining the division of responsibilities.

Further information, including a detailed description of the call procedure and the full eligibility criteria can be found here (in Lithuanian): Kvietimas dvišalio bendradarbiavimo projektams finansuoti - ALF

results.summary: Social Power - Convocatoria 2
results.content: Social Power - Convocatoria 2

beneficiaryAdministration:
Civil society organisations based in Spain are invited to submit proposals under the Social Power project. This call supports initiatives that address three thematic rights agendas: decent employment in a fair productive system, gender justice and diversity and social protection and housing, particularly in contexts of inequality or discrimination. The three thematic rights provide a concrete operational framework to advance fundamental rights and EU values in practice.

-Call publication date: 1 September 2026

-Deadline to submit proposals: 2 November 2026 before 17:00h (CET)

-Full guidelines and application form available at: https://socialpower.es/

Evaluation criteria (maximum score 100 points):

Relevance (maximum 40 points, minimum 25): assessment of the social need, alignment with the call’s priorities, understanding of the rights situation and experience with target groups. An additional 3 bonus points will be awarded to organisations based outside Madrid and Barcelona (municipalities under 1 million inhabitants).

Quality and Coherence (maximum 40 points, minimum 3 points required for the Budget sub-criterion): sound project design, feasibility, gender mainstreaming, clarity of indicators and a realistic budget.

Impact (maximum 20 points): focus on social innovation, empowerment, alliances, participation and influence on public policy.

Only proposals scoring 70 points or more will be considered for funding. Final selection will consider thematic distribution, risk assessment and budget review.

The evaluation process will include automated tools and human oversight. A generative AI tool will support consistency by providing a preliminary analysis based on predefined criteria.

results.summary: Együttható (Civil-Business)
results.content: Együttható (Civil-Business)

beneficiaryAdministration:
Grants, knowledge sharing, networking – Aspektus+ is a complex four-year capacity building programme for rural NGOs in Hungary. The sub-program “Együttható” is for formal, independent, non-profit civil society organizations, established and operating in the 4 core regions of Aspect Group (South Trans-Danubia, South Plains, North Plains, North Hungary). The aim of this program is to motivate CSOs to cooperate with the private sector.

This program helps to find a common language between the two sectors and to engage for-profit organizations to act for social change on the community level. This means fostering active citizenship, stand up for inclusion, ensure represantation of marginalised groups, promoting equality and engaging in solving current challenges from environment protection to the access to services. Beside that, the cooperation will also help CSOs to reach their goals and to become more sustainable. The 16 supported projects set a good example, showing that it is possible to cooperate with the private sector in the countryside. We both support new cooperations and also organizations who have experience in working with companies.

The form of the grant is a lump sum. This amount cannot be less than EUR 3 000 or more than EUR 5 250.

“Együttható” is a multistage call. The first stage is about the formal eligibility of the applicant and the concept. The second stage is about the professional evaluation with 6 award criteria with maximum 5 points each. The awarded projects have to be over 20 points. The professional evaluation will be made by the joint Aspektus committee with 2 members from each organisation. Each concept note and full application will be read by 2 members (one from the region and one from outside). Once the committee has made its decision, the applicants are notified about the results. Applications must be submitted in Hungarian.

results.summary: RIZA Call for proposals
results.content: RIZA Call for proposals

beneficiaryAdministration:
Rooted in the EU founding principles of human dignity, freedom and democracy, RIZA’s main mission is to build capacity of and provide financial support to small-scale grassroots NGOs across the EU to uphold, protect and promote EU values and fundamental rights, focussing on those in most isolated circumstances with least access to resources and opportunities, i.e. migrant and refugee women. With 3 rounds of funding in total (2025, 2026 and 2027), this 2nd RIZA call has a regional focus on the Southern-Mediterranean states (Spain, Portugal, Italy, Greece, Cyprus, Malta) in which the organisations in the region are particularly encouraged to apply, however, RIZA funding is open to any qualified organisations established in any EU members state.

The call is open to the following organisations, Tier 1 constituting the priority group among the potential grantees:

Tier 1: Migrant and/or refugee women led organisations with a human right based mission.

Tier 2: Grassroots women’s rights organisations with a stand-alone programme aimed at supporting migrant and/or refugee women.

Tier 3: Migrant and/or refugee organisations with a stand-alone programme aimed at supporting migrant and/or refugee women.

Tier 4: Grassroots human rights organisations with a stand-alone programme aimed at supporting migrant and/or refugee women.

Call’s Priorities:

•Priority 1: Support and Capacity Building of Migrant and Refugee women

•Priority 2: Advocating for the fundamental rights of migrant and refugee women

•Priority 3: Promoting the role of migrant and refugee women in democratic dialogue, community cohesion and cross-cultural solidarity

For eligible activities under each Priority, please consult detailed information in the call for proposals.

Available grants

•16 Micro Grants of Euro 17778

•12 Small Grants of Euro 32778

•6 Medium Grants of Euro 60000

Application process:  

1 stage: eligibility, admissibility and general relevance.

2 stage: shortlisted candidates only, evaluation of relevance, quality and impact.

An information session is foreseen on: Tuesday 9th June 2026 10:00-12:00 CET

For more information please visit: www.migrantwomennetwork.org/riza

Contact: riza@migrantwomennetwork.org

results.summary: Comprehensive and inclusive support for women and girls' victims of GBV
results.content: Comprehensive and inclusive support for women and girls' victims of GBV

beneficiaryAdministration:
The CoPower Action has been designed to directly fund initiatives addressing Gender Based Violence(GBV) against women, girls and children through an intersectional approach.

All eligible activities supported through the project calls will directly respond to the multidimensional and intersecting needs of women, girls, and child survivors of GBV, strengthening an inclusive and accessible protection systems across different intervention contexts. Child protection and gender mainstreaming are expected to be integral components of the proposals submitted by CSOs, while partner organisations will provide dedicated technical support to improve the capacities of participating CSOs in these areas.

3 NATIONAL CALLS 

Three national calls will support CSOs in Italy, Greece and Spain focusing on: Comprehensive and inclusive support for women and girls' victims of GBV. 

TARGET APPLICANTS 

The calls target small and medium-sized grassroots CSOs, particularly those operating in rural, peripherical or marginalised areas and legally registered in Italy, Greece or Spain. The primary target group, will include Women’s rights organisations (WROs), Anti-violence centres and anti-trafficking centres, Human rights, LGBTIQ+ rights, child rights, social inclusion and disability, elderly, migrant and refugee organisations. 

2 FUNDING WORKSTREAMS: 

1. Enhanced protection response for women, girls and children, victims of GBV, adopting an intersectional approach. This area focusses on providing tailored protection and support services, including safe houses, medical and psychological assistance for women and girls, in all their diversity, who are victims of domestic, sexual violence and other forms of GBV considering specific barriers for equal access to protection (Budget: 540,000 EUR in total for the 3 Countries). 

2. Reduction of harmful practices, with a focus on improving interventions against harmful practices such as female genital mutilation, intersex genital mutilation, forced abortion, forced sterilisation, child and forced marriage, and honour-related violence, forced medicalisation of transgender women. Funded projects will aim at both 9 preventing and responding to these practices, with a particular focus on raising awareness, strengthening legal frameworks, and providing education to communities at risk (Budget: 360,000 EUR in total for the 3 Countries). 

CALL TIMELINE  

First Round: 

  1. Opening: 24/08/2026 (11/09/2026 in Greece) 
  2. Deadline: 23/11/2026 at 15.00 CET 

Second Round: 

  1. Opening: 01/12/2026 
  2. Deadline: 01/03/2027 at 15.00 CET 

 

AVAILABLE GRANT PER COUNTRY: 

First Round - 6 projects of the following amounts will be awarded: 

  1. Stream 1: one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 20,000 
  2. Stream 2: one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 25,000; one grant of EUR 5,000 

Second Round - 4 projects of the following amounts will be awarded: 

  1. Stream 1: one grant of EUR 30,000; one grant of EUR 30,000; 
  2. Stream 2: one grant of EUR 20,000; one grant of EUR 20,000 

APPLICATION PROCESS:  

  1. Administrative check 
  2. Eligibility requirements verification and shortlisting 
  3. Final assessment and selection 
  4. Pre-notification and Due diligence 
  5. Confirmation and signing the agreement 
  6. Information session are foreseen online and in present in each country. 

For more information please visit: https://copower.oxfam.it/ 

Contact: infocopower@oxfam.it

callTitle: Comprehensive and inclusive support for women and girls' victims of GBV
furtherInformation:
The CoPower project is implemented by Oxfam Italia ETS, Action Aid Hellas, Asociación Bienestar y Desarolloa and We World-GVC. It started on 1 March 2026 and will end on 28 February 2029.

Its objective is to strengthen the capacity of Civil Society Organisation (CSOs) to provide safe and inclusive services for victims of gender-based violence (GBV) against women, girls, and children in all their diversity across six European countries: Italy, Greece, Spain, Serbia, Romania, and Albania.

The project foresees three national calls, along with transnational calls involving the following country pairs: Italy–Serbia, Spain-Romania, and Greece-Albania. The national calls will fund at least 10 projects in Italy, 10 in Spain and 10 in Greece. The transnational calls will fund 5 projects for Italy and Serbia, 5 projects for Spain and Romania and 5 projects for Greece and Albania. Overall, a minimum of 60 CSOs will be engaged, fostering meaningful cross-country cooperation.

A comprehensive capacity-sharing programme for CSOs will include needs assessments, training, mentoring, and both national and international workshops to promote mutual learning and support in the full implementation of the EU Violence Against Women Directive.

title: Strengthening the remembrance of Roma victims
descriptionByte:
Objective:

3. Strengthening the remembrance of the Holocaust, acts of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity to strengthen democracy in the EU.

Projects under this topic should focus on the non-Jewish victims of the Holocaust as well as other genocides, war crimes and crimes against humanity of the 20th century’s Europe.

Projects under this topic should NOT address the Holocaust against Jewish people which are covered by Topic 2.

CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM-GENCRIME-1 - Priority 1: Strengthening the remembrance of Roma victims

The genocide of Roma and Sinti under Nazi rule, known as Porajmos or Samudaripen, is a defining yet insufficiently recognized legacy for the European Union. An estimated 500,000 Roma, including Sinti and Travellers, were murdered, and countless others were persecuted, deported, forcibly sterilized, and subjected to inhuman treatment. The Nazi regime implemented racial policies aimed at the systematic destruction of Roma communities across Europe, culminating in mass killings such as the liquidation of the Roma camp at Auschwitz-Birkenau on 2 August 1944, now commemorated as European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day.

The Roma Holocaust must be understood within a longer continuum of antigypsyism in Europe. Roma were enslaved for nearly five centuries in the territories of present-day Romania, deprived of legal personhood and basic rights. In the 20th century, persecution continued under fascist and communist regimes and, in several countries, through forced sedentarisation, assimilation policies, and coercive practices including forced sterilizations. These historical injustices have had lasting socio-economic consequences.

Despite this, Roma persecution remains underrepresented in school curricula, museums, and public memorials. Dedicated research centres, permanent monuments, and teaching materials on Roma history and the Roma Holocaust are limited. This structural invisibility contributes to persistent antigypsyism, distortion, and denial.

As survivor numbers decline, preserving testimonies, memorial sites, and archival materials becomes increasingly urgent. Commemorative initiatives such as 2 August – European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day – and 16 May – Romani Resistance Day require stronger institutional support and integration into European remembrance culture.

Current political developments also demonstrate the vulnerability of Roma Holocaust memory. Historical distortion, trivialization, and denial — often intertwined with broader antigypsyist narratives — undermine democratic values. Memory competition and selective recognition of victimhood risk reinforcing exclusion. Citizens must be empowered to counter distortion, denial, and the minimization of the Roma genocide. In line with the EU Roma Strategic Framework for Equality Inclusion and Participation 2020-2030, special priority will be given to projects that strengthen Roma Holocaust remembrance while addressing the deeper roots of antigypsyism.

Projects under this priority could focus on:

  • Documenting the implementation of the Roma genocide and its historical context, including slavery, post-war persecution and totalitarian persecutions.
  • Countering denial, distortion, trivialization, and the marginalization of Roma victimhood.
  • Developing networks of Roma and non-Roma youth ambassadors to promote remembrance and counter antigypsyism.
  • Supporting grassroots commemorative initiatives, including activities marking 2 August – European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day, 16 May – Romani Resistance Day, etc.
  • Developing and disseminating teaching materials that integrate Roma history and the Roma Holocaust into national curricula.
  • Digitalizing testimonies, archival documents, and historical research to preserve memory for future generations.
  • Promoting research on Roma restitution, forced displacement, and long-term consequences of historical injustice.
  • Collecting, documenting and disseminating stories of Roma resistance, heroes, rescuers, intellectuals, artists and community leaders, highlighting Roma agency, resilience and contribution to European history.
  • Applying transitional justice approaches, including truth-seeking, recognition of harm, restitution research, and guarantees of non-repetition through education and memorialization.
  • Developing inclusive, participatory ways to remember, educate about, and teach about these crimes in order to prevent the resurgence of hatred, including antigypsyism. This may include artistic memory projects, memory activism, and other approaches that foster an enabling learning environment.

For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the Call document.

title: Strengthening the remembrance of LGBTIQ+ victims and other victims
descriptionByte:
Objective:

3. Strengthening the remembrance of the Holocaust, acts of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity to strengthen democracy in the EU.

Projects under this topic should focus on the non-Jewish victims of the Holocaust as well as other genocides, war crimes and crimes against humanity of the 20th century’s Europe.

Projects under this topic should NOT address the Holocaust against Jewish people which are covered by Topic 2.

CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM-GENCRIME-2 - Priority 2: Strengthening the remembrance of LGBTIQ+ victims and other victims

Projects under this priority should not address projects focusing on the remembrance of Roma victims (Projects focussing on the remembrance of Roma victims should apply under Priority 1).

Europe’s 20th century was marked by horrific crimes, genocides, war crimes and crimes against humanity as well as the crimes committed under authoritarian and totalitarian regimes, including those of communist and fascist dictatorships. The remembrance of these gravest crimes committed on European soil plays a critical role in upholding these values.

Despite growing efforts to preserve the memory of the victims of these crimes, the experiences of many groups remain overlooked, marginalised or insufficiently recognised in public memory. This includes, among others, LGBTIQ+ people and other communities targeted on the basis of their identity, beliefs or perceived social status.

Throughout history, LGBTIQ+ people have faced systemic persecution under a wide range of political and social regimes, often shaped by prevailing religious, cultural, and legal norms. Under the Nazi regime, it is estimated that 50000 gay and bisexual men were subject to ‘severe jail sentences in brutal conditions’, with around 10-15000 being sent to concentration camps. Lesbian women, transgender people, and others whose identities did not conform to Nazi ideals of gender and sexuality also faced surveillance, discrimination, violence, and social exclusion, with their experiences largely unrecognized for decades.

As a result, the history of LGBTIQ+ persons in Europe is marked by both struggle and resilience. The preservation and recognition of LGBTIQ+ history and memory are essential to building an inclusive European identity rooted in dignity, diversity, and human rights. Remembering and recognising these atrocities is essential to restore justice as underlined in the LGBTIQ+ equality strategy 2026-2030.

Greater awareness of all these histories contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of the causes, mechanisms and consequences of mass atrocities and contributes not only to preventing their recurrence but also to reinforcing democratic resilience, fostering civic engagement, and building a common European culture of remembrance.

Projects under this topic could focus on:

  • Addressing how genocides, war crimes and crimes against humanity were organised, which actors were involved and how they were committed, the roles of collaborators, perpetrators and bystanders.
  • Finding new ways of remembering, educating and teaching about these crimes to protect society against resurging threats of hatred. They can include artistic work on memory projects, as well as stimulating memory activism. These new methods should be inclusive, where applicable participatory and create an enabling learning environment.
  • Fostering awareness raising, mutual learning or training activities that accurately reflect the persecution of LGBTIQ+ people, and other minorities throughout history.
  • Countering historical falsification and memory competition related to the persecution of LGBTIQ+ people, genocides, war crimes and crimes against humanity, especially among Europeans that shared a common history but have divergent views on their common past.
  • Fostering awareness raising, mutual learning or training activities that accurately reflect the persecution of LGBTIQ+ people, and other minorities under the Nazi regime while countering denial, distortion, trivialization, and especially false comparisons.
  • Addressing divergent and opposite national historical narratives, on regional basis, of these darkest hours of Europe history and other negative common shared historical events.
  • Digitalising historical material and testimonies of witnesses for education and training purposes.

For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the Call document.

4. CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM-HISTMIGRATION - Fostering remembrance of the legacy of colonialism, slavery, and migration, and their impact on contemporary multicultural European societies.

Migration, de-colonisation, enslavement, and imperialism have left a mark on global history and are embedded in the European history, with profound consequences for society today. Their remembrance plays a key role in combating structural racism, empowering people impacted by racism, and raising awareness of exclusion and stereotypes.

While for many it is considered a chapter in history, de-colonisation, the dismantlement of colonial empires particularly in the 20th century and the emerging post-colonial European societies continue to have harsh consequences in the lives of people facing racism and racial discrimination. Following the decolonisation process in international relations in the early 20th century, the UN World Conference on Combating Racism, Racial Discrimination, and Xenophobia established that today’s structural inequalities are caused by the consequences of colonialism and slavery.

Stemming from this observation, in its EU Anti-Racism Action Plan 2020-2025 and EU Anti-Racism Strategy 2026–2030, the Commission made efforts to communicate on addressing the historical roots of racism and established a key priority to combat structural racism. This entails an examination of the past, present and future of the cultural fabric of Europe. Prejudices and stereotypes can be addressed by acknowledging the historical roots of racism, including from an intersectional perspective.

Migration has also a long and varied history in Europe. Population movements in Europe, from economic, political migration to expulsion and deportation after the Second World War, from fleeing violence and persecution to migration after the creation of the EU, have marked 20th century European history. Forced migration, internal displacement and expulsion is an experience shared by many Europeans during the period of war. This includes the forced displacement and persecution of Roma populations during and after the Second World War, and its long-term consequences. The specific history of female migration can also be considered.

Projects in this priority should contribute to a better understanding of how these historical legacies - rooted in colonialism, enslavement an imperialism - shape contemporary inequalities, discrimination, exclusion and barriers to equal opportunities in European societies. Projects are encouraged to examine the links between these historical legacies and contemporary manifestations of structural racism, including anti-Black racism, antigypsyism, antisemitism, anti-Muslim hatred and anti-Asian racism.

Projects under this topic could focus on:

  • Acknowledging the legacy of colonialism and its ongoing impact on contemporary multicultural European societies, with a view to contributing to the objectives of the EU Anti-Racism Strategy 2026–2030, including addressing topics such as structural discrimination and racism.
  • Promoting anti-racism education, historical literacy and awareness-raising initiatives aimed at young people, educators and wider society, including through innovative and participatory approaches that foster mutual respect, inclusion and democratic values.
  • Supporting the collection, preservation and dissemination of testimonies, archives and community-based knowledge that contribute to a stronger evidence base on the historical roots and contemporary manifestations of racism and discrimination in Europe.
  • Raising awareness of Roma history and culture to contribute to strengthening multicultural European societies, in line with the EU Roma Strategic Framework for equality, inclusion and participation.
  • Examining common European experiences of migration linked to historical events such as wars, transition moments, colonisation and de-colonisation, economic impacts, or persecution.

Adopting an intersectional approach to cover several minority groups, including People of African descent, Jews, Roma, overseas citizens, and other minority groups with a long history of migration, to promote a more nuanced understanding of multicultural European societies.

For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the Call document.

title: Strengthening the remembrance of the Holocaust against Jewish people.
descriptionByte:
Objective:

2. CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM-HOLOCAUSTJEW - Strengthening the remembrance of the Holocaust against Jewish people.

The Shoah is a defining legacy for the EU. Six million Jewish children, women and men were murdered, and all others were persecuted. While other groups were persecuted, the Nazis have set up across Europe and beyond a state policy with the sole aim to kill every single Jews they could find.

First-hand accounts of the Shoah continue to have the most powerful impact on following generations. As there are less and less survivors to share the story of their survival, the importance of memorial sites and education increases, as well as the work done by second and third generations of survivors and associations.

Current events show the instrumentalization of the Holocaust by Kremlin propaganda claiming to denazify Ukraine. In parallel, there is also an increasing politicization of the Holocaust in several EU Member States, and a tendency to minimize the atrocities of the Shoah. In addition, since the 7 October 2023 attacks by Hamas and the wars that ensued, we have seen a growing conflation of the Shoah with the conflicts in the Middle East. Citizens should be empowered to counter this conflation.

Holocaust distortion fuels antisemitism. In addition, hate speech relating to the condoning, denial or gross trivialisation of the Holocaust is criminalised under the Council Framework Decision on combating certain forms and expressions of racism and xenophobia by means of criminal law4.

Wounds of mass atrocities of the 20th century are still open today, fuelling divergences among Europeans. Free, open and independent research, education and memory on all aspects of the Shoah is essential to increase understanding. This implies exploring Europe’s negative history with the aim to reconcile divergent regional and national narratives related to the Shoah and its immediate aftermath.

European citizens should become ambassadors of this memory. Teachers, policymakers, university students (especially history students) could be among key target audiences and be empowered to develop a common European history, to counter historical falsification, distortion and inversion. Target groups could include local public authorities and policy makers, to raise awareness about their responsibility to safeguard the sites and combat antisemitism. Target groups could include newcomers and migrants that do not have a direct link with the Shoah. Target groups could also include journalists, to raise awareness about Holocaust distortion, Holocaust inversion and Holocaust-related contemporary events (such as for example Neo-Nazi marches).

In line with the EU Strategy on combating antisemitism and fostering Jewish life (2021-2030), as well as with other key policy initiatives, this topic supports projects that can focus on developing networks of Young European Ambassadors to promote Shoah remembrance. This topic will also support projects that contribute to Holocaust sites especially regarding their educational purposes, and encourage cooperation with ESHEM, the network of European Sites of Holocaust Memory. Jewish communities are today small, as a direct consequence from the Holocaust. This results in direct responsibility to support Jewish life and raise awareness about Jewish presence in Europe.

Projects under this topic could focus on:

  • Addressing how the Shoah took place, how the crimes were committed, which actors were involved, as well as pre-war and immediate postwar historical developments.
  • Countering Holocaust denial, distortion, trivialisation and victims’ inversion. This includes countering false comparisons, antisemitic conspiracy theories, and conflation with the Middle East conflict.
  • Monitoring and countering on the online sphere Holocaust distortion and inversion, as well as Nazi glorification. Addressing divergent and opposite national historical narratives, on regional basis, of the history of the Shoah, including parallelism with other negative common shared historical regional events.
  • Promoting memory activism related to the Shoah including by supporting grassroot commemorative work.
  • Digitalising historical material and testimonies of witnesses for education and training purposes.
  • Shedding light on Jewish life before and after the Shoah.
  • Raising awareness on Jewish life, history and culture, to contribute to strengthening multicultural European societies.
  • Marking International Holocaust Remembrance Day and national Holocaust remembrance days.
  • Raise awareness on the Shoah and memorial sites at local level, including through visits of local authorities. Combating glorification of Nazism, countering neo-Nazis manifestations and activities.
  • Promoting provenance research on looted art to foster awareness raising, mutual learning or training activities.

For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the Call document.

4 Council Framework Decision 2008/913/JHA of 28 November 2008 on combating certain forms and expressions of racism and xenophobia by means of criminal law, EUR-Lex - 32008F0913 - EN - EUR-Lex

title: Remembering democratic transitions, the (re-)building of democratic institutions, and strengthening society based on the rule of law, democracy, and fundamental rights.
descriptionByte:
Objective:

1. CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM-TRANSITION - Remembering democratic transitions, the (re-)building of democratic institutions, and strengthening society based on the rule of law, democracy, and fundamental rights.

The EU is a community of values, and all its Member States committed to respect the principles of democracy, the rule of law, and respect for fundamental rights. Europe's experiences in the 20th century demonstrates the need for resilient democracies and the need for people to actively engage in and protect democratic institutions and values. Historical experience such as in the 1920s and 1930s, when some European democracies went through particularly challenging times, are stark reminders of the importance to promote democracy, also in a historical perspective. Today, democracy faces several challenges, which underlined the need to strengthen public trust in democratic processes and institutions and to recall the importance of democracy in people’s daily life.

Democratic transitions (defined as the transition from a non-democratic to a democratic system, a transition undertaken by several European countries before joining the EU) are not only political and legal processes but also societal transformations.The transition and consolidation of democracies through institutional and legal reforms have been essential. In addition, delivering justice to victims and affected communities after the fall of totalitarian and authoritarian regimes (including communist and fascist dictatorships) can aid in societal healing, bolster and reinforce resilience against present and future threats to democracies.

Projects under this topic can focus on:

  • The ongoing development and nurturing of democracies in the context of past transitions from authoritarian and totalitarian regimes (including communist and fascist dictatorships) across various European countries, reveals important lessons for defending and upholding EU values such as democracy, the rule of law, and fundamental rights.
  • They can also reflect on both shared patterns and national specificities, while underlining the lasting impact of the totalitarian or authoritarian past, and how its difficult legacy continues to be remembered, interpreted, and engaged with today.
  • Examining and giving visibility to acts of resistance and organised opposition to past totalitarian and authoritarian regimes, as part of the ongoing effort to nurture and protect democracy in the face of enduring and emerging challenges.
  • Transition from authoritarian and totalitarian regimes (including communist and fascist dictatorships) towards democracy.
  • Promoting remembrance and education about past events in which fundamental rights such as freedom of expression, assembly, thought, conscience, religion, and electoral rights were suppressed under past totalitarian and authoritarian regimes. These examples serve to reinforce the importance of protecting democratic values today, including the right to express dissenting opinions and ensuring a political space where opposition voices can be freely and safely heard.
  • Exploring the means of historical justice, be it through trials, restitution or amnesty, and possibility still today to work on restorative justice.

The elements described above to strengthen democracies, such as fighting foreign interference, including the manipulation and falsification of historical facts, strengthen citizen engagement, critical thinking, media literacy, and societal resilience, are closely related to the context of remembrance, as they help ensure that the dramatic events of the past are not repeated in contemporary Europe.

For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the Call document.

results.summary: Internationalisation Supports to Emirats for SMEs
results.content: Internationalisation Supports to Emirats for SMEs

beneficiaryAdministration:
SMEs located in COSME countries, which are members of the project Clusters* or in a process of becoming members and that are interested in strengthening their international capacity in the target countries of F2F Health Matters and the following areas: i) Innovative & Sustainable Healthy Food, ii) Bio-based Techno-functional Ingredients & Solutions and iii) Bio-solutions -- to become more global across overseas markets of connected food, the market of functional food and healthy ingredient, the market of processed food products, can apply for support.

An initial eligibility check will be conducted following the criteria established in the call. All applicants will be notified about the eligibility verification. Eligible applicants will be notified they have been shortlisted and will proceed to the evaluation step. The project will conduct an assessment of the export readiness of the applicants, to assess the applicant company, the product/service, presence in international markets, organisation and management for internationalisation.

For further information on the selection criteria, please consult our website: https://f2f-project.eu/get-involved/

For the selected SMEs, an agreement will be signed between the corresponding Cluster and the beneficiary SME detailing the rights and obligations of both parties.

*F2F Health Matters is operated by Wagralim (BE), Valorial (FR), Clusaga (ES), InovCluster (PT) and Bioeconomy Cluster Slovakia (SK)

/!\ The F2F Health Matters team has forseen 3 calls in total, meaning one for Canada (already closed), one for Japan (already closed) and one for UAE (current call). The total funding available for the 3 calls is 105 000€, after the Canada and Japan call, 37 000€ is left for Emirats.

results.summary: EFFEA Call #5
results.content: EFFEA Call #5

beneficiaryAdministration:
The European Festivals Fund for Emerging Artists – EFFEA, an initiative of the European Festivals Association, is a fund that supports collaborations between festivals from different countries. Together, these festivals provide emerging artists with a platform to develop their work and gain visibility on the international stage. EFFEA extends an open invitation for festivals to collaborate across borders and establish a network of colleagues centred around the concept of a residency. Through EFFEA, festivals join hands to foster the success of emerging artists.

EFFEA's fifth call for festivals to support emerging artists is open from 1 September to 3 November 2026. 50 residencies will be selected involving 50 emerging artists (individuals, groups or collectives) in the seat of around 150 festivals, a leading festival in collaboration with a minimum of two partner festivals each.

There are two categories of residencies:

1. EFFEA Discovery: Festivals support artists at the early stages of their careers but with a strong potential to break through internationally. 40 grants of 8.000€ will be attributed to this category.

2. EFFEA Springboard: Festivals support artists already established in their own country and ready to develop their careers internationally. 10 grants of 15.000€ will be attributed to this category.

Eligibility criteria

  1. The partnership must represent at least 3 festivals from 3 eligible countries (1 leading festival and 2 partner festivals).
  2. Both leading and partner festivals must exist for at least one edition.
  3. Both leading and partner festivals must be registered on www.FestivalFinder.eu before submitting their application.
  4. A festival may apply for one grant as a leading festival and is eligible to apply for multiple grants as a partner festival.
  5. Proposed artists may be individual artists, collectives, companies, ensembles, or groups of any age and nationality.
  6. Artists must have either nationality or legal residence in one of the eligible countries.

Eligible Countries   

Leading festivals and artists should have their official address in one of the following eligible countries: Albania, Armenia, Austria, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Georgia, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Kosovo, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Montenegro, Moldova, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Tunisia, Ukraine.

Festivals with their official address from the following countries are allowed to participate as partner festivals only: Israel, Palestine, Switzerland, Turkey, and the UK. Artists from these countries can also be proposed.

Eligible disciplines

Festivals and artists work in one or more of the following artistic disciplines: Architecture, Ballet, Contemporary Dance, Circus, Design/ Applied arts, Digital arts, Film, Folklore and folk arts, Heritage, Interdisciplinary, Literature, Music, Opera, Street Art, Theatre, Photography/ Video, Puppetry, Sculpture, Painting.

Conditions and Selection Criteria

The start and end dates of the residency must fall within the implementation period. This means that the residency start date must be no earlier than 1 January 2027, and the end date must be no later than 31 December 2027. If applicants start the residency earlier or end it later, any costs related to the extended period must not be included in the budget submitted to EFFEA.

Submitted proposals will be assessed for eligibility by the EFA team. All eligible proposals will be evaluated by the EFFEA Jury, composed of members with diverse profiles in terms of artistic disciplines, geographies, backgrounds, gender, age, and, above all, with knowledge of the arts field.

The selection criteria assume that: 

  1. The residency is relevant for the artists, festivals and audiences. 
  2. It will have an impact on the artists’ careers. 
  3. It offers a market to artists even beyond the residency period (longer term). 
  4. The budget is built on the principle of fair remuneration towards the artists at all stages (stay, rehearsal time and payment, fees, etc.). 
  5. The topics of today focus on diversity, sustainability (ecological, cultural, artistic, economic and social), digital tools and inclusion. These can be cited as motivation and will be considered in evaluating the quality of the residency. 

Submission

The leading festival must submit the application online via the EFFEA website. Applications cannot be submitted in any other way.

The leading festival will be asked to fill in:

  1. General information about leading festival/ organisation.
  2. Information about the proposed artists, including short biographies and links (text and/or audiovisual).
  3. General information about the partner festivals.
  4. Motivation for supporting the artists and establishing the partnership for the residency.
  5. Letter of intent with the artists (template available for download).
  6. Letter of intent with the partner festivals (template available for download).
  7. A detailed budget form (template available to download).

The Leading Festivals must

  1. Upload and sign all required documents (including the budget and letters of intent with the artists and the partner festivals).
  2. Ensure that the proposed residency dates fall within the eligible implementation period.
  3. Ensure that the proposed artists meet the EFFEA eligibility criteria regarding previous participation.

Artists who received a Discovery grant through a previous EFFEA Call remain eligible for a Springboard residency under Call #5.

Applications will be evaluated in November 2026. Applicants will be notified of the results by email in December 2026.

beneficiaryAdministration:
IZOLYATSIA Foundation (UA) and Malý Berlín (SK) together with Trans Europe Halles (SE) announce the rolling open call for cultural and arts organisations within the ZMINA:Resilience project, strand "Support for international showcasing of co-creation projects".

The objective of this call is to support projects that bring artistic and cultural works co-created by Ukrainian and other Creative Europe cultural organisations to wider audiences through public showcasing and presentation events in Ukraine and across other Creative Europe countries.

Funding will be provided to projects featuring co-creations made by partnerships involving at least one organisation from Ukraine and at least one organisation from another Creative Europe country. The projects should maximise the visibility, audience reach, sustainability, and future showcasing potential of these works.

Supported projects are expected to include active partner cooperation to adapt showcased works to new audiences, for example by contextualising works, providing translation, involving local artists, experts and communities, conducting parallel programmes, and similar approaches.

All creative and cultural sectors are eligible except audiovisual.

Project Objectives

  1. Showcase and tour co-creations that explore the theme of resilience in any arts or cultural sector except audiovisual.
  2. Hold a minimum of 6 public presentation events: at least 3 events in each of at least two countries, one of which must be Ukraine.
  3. The presentation events cannot take place in the home city or town of any of the applicant organisations.

Overall Strand Budget

Total funding available: 950,000 €

Grant amount: up to 50,000 €, covering up to 90% of total project costs.

The remaining 10% must be covered by the applicants as their own contribution in monetary form (not in-kind) and reflected in their accounting statements.

Expected number of grants: 19–25.

Rolling Call — Selection Rounds

This is a rolling call, open for 16 months, with deadlines every three or four months (see indicative timeline). Applications are reviewed and selected after every round deadline.

The rolling structure allows applicants to submit proposals for showcasing projects that are ready to go immediately, as well as those requiring more preparation time — including projects that received co-creation funding through earlier ZMINA:Resilience calls.

Who Can Apply?

Organisations working in the arts and culture sectors, registered in Creative Europe countries (EU countries and non-EU countries).

For Ukraine — registered in territories under the effective control of the Ukrainian government.

While proposals are submitted by a single lead applicant, the project must include at least two partner organisations from at least two countries, one of which is Ukraine. All partners have equal rights and joint responsibility for the correctness of data submitted on the platform and in future reporting.

The partnership must reflect genuine balance and exchange — not a formality. Each partner should play an equally important role, bring equal value, and contribute to reaching audiences in all participating countries.

Eligible Activities

  1. All activities necessary for the preparation and delivery of the presentation events, including:
  2. Public presentation events (in Ukraine, hybrid or online formats are accepted due to the security situation)
  3. Preparation, rehearsals, and production activities related to the presentations
  4. Travel for organisational, rehearsal, and presentation purposes

All projects must include at least 3 presentation events in each of at least 2 countries, one of which must be Ukraine. Presentation events cannot take place in the home city or town of any of the applicant organisations

Eligible Costs

  1. All costs necessary for the implementation of the project
  2. Costs of presenting artistic and cultural works in each partner's country
  3. Travel related to organisational, rehearsal, creative, and presentation purposes

All costs must be incurred after the grant agreement is signed and during the implementation period.

Project Duration

The implementation period is up to 7 months. The earliest start of implementation is after signing the grant agreement.

Technical Eligibility Criteria

  1. All required attachments are uploaded in separate files in the formats specified for this call.
  2. All required attachments follow standard templates available for download on the platform.
  3. All required attachments are readable, accessible, and printable.
  4. All project partners meet the eligibility conditions for this call.
  5. The applicant's registration meets the conditions specified for this call.
  6. The application form is complete and contains all requested information.
  7. The application is submitted by the eligible lead applicant.
  8. The subgrant amount requested does not exceed the maximum set for this call.
  9. The total partner contribution meets the co-financing requirements.
  10. The project implementation period is within the limits set for this call.
  11. The project start date meets the conditions specified for this call.

Applications are checked for technical eligibility by the ZMINA:Resilience team. Proposals found admissible and eligible are forwarded to evaluators (2 per application).

Evaluation Criteria

Relevance:

Relevance of the project to the objectives of this call.

Quality:

Quality of the partnership — equal importance of the roles played by each partner.

Extent to which cross-cutting issues (digital dimension, environmental sustainability, inclusion) and barrier-free access to project results are addressed.

Scale of engagement — expected audience size and number of presentation events.

Impact:

Sustainability of the project, including plans for future showcasing and presentations beyond the grant period.

Selection Procedure

Applications are first reviewed for technical eligibility by the ZMINA:Resilience team to confirm compliance with all formal requirements, including eligibility and admissibility criteria.

Proposals that pass this stage are forwarded to two independent experts for evaluation. Evaluators assign scores, after which applications are ranked by average score.

Final selection is made by the Selection Committee, taking into account geographical, sectoral, and thematic diversity within the available call budget.

The application budget is assessed for cost-effectiveness and justification and may be adjusted prior to signing the grant agreement. The final grant amount is determined based on a combination of lump-sum units and actually incurred costs.

Due to the volume of applications received, the ZMINA:Resilience project team will not be able to provide individual justification for selection decisions. All decisions are final.

How to Apply

Via the IZOLYATSIA online platform, no later than 23:59 (Kyiv time) on the last day of the corresponding selection round: https://platform.izolyatsia.org

The application is submitted by ONE representative of the consortium (the lead applicant).

Language of application: English.

Required Documents

The application package includes:

Application form and budget (filled in directly on the platform).

Supporting documents on capacity, eligibility, and admissibility — uploaded in .pdf format separately for each partner:

Scanned copy of the guarantee letter, completed and signed by the head of the organisation (template available for download on the platform).

Registration documents:

For organisations from Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine — national registration documents with an English translation if the original is in another language.

For organisations from Ukraine — a full extract from the Unified State Register of Legal Entities, Individual Entrepreneurs and Public Organisations, dated after the announcement of this call — in the original language.

Current Statute or equivalent document (if required for the legal entity) — all pages:

For organisations from Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine — with an English translation if the original is in another language.

For organisations from Ukraine — in the original language.

Note: The application form, the budget, the guarantee letter, other supporting documents, and any information the applicant provides to ZMINA:Resilience team are not the mere formality. Where those or any parts thereof are untrue, factually inaccurate, misleading, unfounded, misrepresent the facts, lack factual basis, and the like, providing support to the projects can be terminated at any stage of their lifecycle.
