1. Aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships

The aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships (hereinafter referred to as the SCHOLARSHIPS) is to support students in completing their full curriculum through a triple degree programme at the University of Pavia and the University of Vaasa, thereby extending their knowledge and skills in advanced digital technologies (one of the DIGI-ME target areas). 

2. DIGI-ME Scholarships 

The SCHOLARSHIPS are granted by the DIGI-ME project. The DIGI-ME project is co-funded by the European Union under Grant Agreement No. 101123009. Up to EUR 100,000 is available to be distributed through targeted scholarships at Grenoble Ecole de Management (hereinafter referred to as GEM). Through this call, up to ten (10) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their participation in the DIGI-ME path of the triple degree programme with the University of Pavia and the University of Vaasa. 

3. Financial value 

3.1 Scholarships are provided as a lump sum to support students in paying their tuition fees during the triple degree exchange programme. Each selected beneficiary will receive a lump sum for two mobility periods totalling 8 to 10 months, depending on the individual Learning Agreement, in the period from January 2027 to May 2027 at the University of Pavia (Italy) and from January 2028 to May 2028 at the University of Vaasa (Finland). 

The scholarship comprises a minimum of one component (Item A) and a maximum of two components (Items A and B). 

3.1.1 Fixed component 

Item A: Total contribution towards tuition fees: EUR 8,000 (one-time payment). 

3.1.2 Additional component based on special conditions 

Item B: Additional contribution towards tuition fees for participants with fewer opportunities: EUR 2,000 (one-time payment). 

Participants with fewer opportunities are defined as students who, prior to the start of the mobility period, meet one or more of the following criteria: 

  1. Are recipients of the French national student grant (CROUS) and belong to one of the four highest grant levels (levels 4, 5, 6, or 7); 
  2. Have a disability with a certified degree of invalidity of at least 50%; 
  3. Hold refugee status and/or benefit from international or subsidiary protection, or are displaced persons; 
  4. Have dependent minor children (students who have given birth to a child during the 2026–2027 academic year, as proven by a birth certificate, up to the child’s first birthday); 
  5. Are engaged in employment (students employed, other than occasionally and not by a family member up to and including the second degree, for a period of at least six months within the 12 months preceding the mobility period, in documented employment, self-employment, or professional activity in the public or private sector); 
  6. Are recognised professional athletes (students who are athletes of national interest must present a certificate from the relevant sports federation); 
  7. Are orphans of at least one parent (a student is considered an orphan if their father and/or mother died before the date of submission of the mobility application. This status is recognised provided that the student: (a) is under 26 years of age at the time of application, and/or (b) was financially dependent on the deceased parent at the time of death or is in a similarly economically dependent situation); 
  8. Are children of victims of terrorism or organised crime. 

Supporting documents for Item B will be requested only from successful applicants. 

4. Payment mechanism 

4.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is paid in two instalments: 

4.1.1 The first instalment, equal to 80% of the total estimated scholarship amount, will be paid within 30 days of signing the Mobility Agreement, provided that the student: 

  1. Has submitted a Learning Agreement duly approved and signed by GEM and the host Higher Education Institution; 
  2. Has correctly entered their bank details in the designated system. 

If any of the above conditions are not met, payment of the first instalment will be made within 30 days of their fulfilment. 

4.1.2 The second instalment, representing the remaining 20%, will be paid at the end of the mobility period, subject to verification of: 

  1. Fulfilment of the administrative and procedural obligations set out in this call; 
  2. Successful completion of the authorised mobility period; 
  3. Achievement of learning outcomes consistent with the Learning Agreement; 
  4. Proper administrative completion of the mobility period. 

Failure to comply with any of the above conditions may result in the loss of entitlement to the final payment and may lead to the total or partial recovery of sums already received. 

Acceptance of the mobility period constitutes a formal commitment by the candidate. Consequently, cancellations must be limited to serious and duly documented cases of force majeure. Any cancellation must be communicated in writing to the DIGI-ME Coordinator (digi-me@unipv.it), with GEM Global – DIGI-ME Section (digime.mobility@grenoble-em.com) in copy, adequately justified, and submitted promptly. Cancellation entails the refund of any financial contributions already received. The reason for cancellation and/or failure to communicate it may be considered when assessing eligibility for future GEM international mobility programmes. 

4.2 Tax treatment 

4.2.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is awarded exclusively to support participation in the triple degree mobility programme. The scholarship is intended to contribute to tuition and mobility-related expenses and does not constitute remuneration for employment, services, or research activities. 

4.2.2 Under French tax legislation, grants awarded to support studies and educational mobility are generally not treated as employment income where they are not paid in exchange for work or services. The DIGI-ME scholarship is awarded solely for educational purposes and does not create any employment relationship between GEM and the beneficiary. 

4.2.3 The tax treatment of the scholarship ultimately depends on the individual circumstances of each beneficiary and on the applicable legislation in force at the time of payment. Beneficiaries are solely responsible for determining any personal tax obligations and, where necessary, for making any required declarations to the competent tax authorities. 

4.2.4 GEM does not provide tax advice and accepts no liability for the individual tax treatment of the scholarship. Applicants are encouraged to consult the French tax authorities or a qualified tax adviser if they require guidance regarding their personal tax situation. For more information, please refer to the French tax administration impots.gouv.fr or service-public.fr. 

5. Evaluation process 

Applications must be submitted EXCLUSIVELY through the dedicated form from 18 September 2026 (09:00, Brussels time) to 18 November 2026 (18:00, Brussels time). A complete list of applicants will be compiled, including basic information for statistical and transparency purposes, and may be shared with the European Commission. Applications that pass the eligibility check will undergo an internal evaluation, conducted by a panel of three experts from GEM. For more information on the selection and evaluation process, please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants (Annex 1). The outcome of the call for awarding the DIGI-ME scholarship will be published on the GEM DIGI-ME page. 

6. Eligibility criteria 

The following applicants are eligible: 

6.1 Students regularly enrolled in one of the following DIGI-ME master’s programmes at Grenoble Ecole de Management: 

  1. MSc Managing with Data and Artificial Intelligence; 
  2. MSc in Innovation and Entrepreneurship; 
  3. MSc in Management in International Business; 

Applicants must be: 

  1. Enrolled for the academic year 2026–2027;
  2. Full-time students; 
  3. Not on academic leave. 

6.2 Citizens of the European Union (hereinafter referred to as the EU) or of eligible DEP countries (the full list is available here: list-3rd-country-participation_digital_en.pdf). 

6.3 Proficiency in English is a fundamental requirement, as English is the official language of both the Open Call and the master’s programmes. 

Unless the applicant is a native English speaker, they must provide evidence meeting one of the following minimum requirements: 

  1. TOEFL iBT: 80; 
  2. IELTS Academic / IELTS Indicator: 6.0; 
  3. Cambridge English (Proficiency, Advanced, or Business Higher): Grade A, B, or C; 
  4. Duolingo English Test: 100; 
  5. Bachelor’s degree fully taught in English (official proof required). 

6.4 According to European Union’s rules, it is forbidden to receive double support for the same incurred costs. Hence, the scholarship covered by this call is incompatible with any other EU funding allocated for the same purpose. Applicants must declare that they have not received other European Union funding for the same purpose in the dedicated form. 

7. Required documents 

7.1 Transcripts of records: Transcripts for the passed exams and related grades (If the student has been studying at a foreign educational institution during the academic year 2025-2026, the study merits have to be provided according to existing regulations and practices of Grenoble Ecole de Management). 

7.2 Curriculum vitae (CV): detailed CV outlining academic history, professional experience, skills, and relevant achievements (no photo required; maximum 1 page). 

7.3 Personal statement / motivation letter: statement (maximum 2 pages) explaining the applicant’s motivation, interest in the programme, and how their background aligns with the DIGI-ME path of the triple degree programme together with the University of Pavia (Italy) and the University of Vaasa (Finland). 

7.4 English language competency: certified evidence of English proficiency meeting the specified minimum scores above. 

7.5 Copy of passport or ID card: copy of a valid passport or identity card. 

7.6 Optional: information on gender, age, and socio-economic status. In the event of equal scores, these factors may be positively considered during evaluation, in line with GEM’s commitment to supporting a diverse student body. 

8. Evaluation criteria and scoring 

8.1 Only eligible candidates will be evaluated. Successful candidates must reach an evaluation threshold of 70%. 

8.2 Applications will be assessed as follows: 

  1. Academic background (65%): based on the weighted average grade and adjusted by the ratio of earned to expected ECTS credits. 
  2. Motivation (25%): reflects the applicant’s commitment to developing advanced digital skills in innovation, international business, and entrepreneurship, as demonstrated in the motivation letter. 
  3. Additional experience (10%): considers academic and non-academic achievements reported in the applicant’s CV. 

8.3 DIGI-ME and GEM are committed to promoting diversity, social and economic equality, and gender balance in all aspects of this open call. As part of our selection process, applicants will have the option to provide information on gender, age, and socio-economic background. In the event of equal scores, priority will be given in the following order: 

  1. Female applicants; 
  2. Applicants from low socio-economic backgrounds; 
  3. Applicants with disabilities; 
  4. Applicants from countries with a low Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI) score; 
  5. Applicants belonging to minority groups. 

8.4 All information provided regarding gender, age, and social background will be collected voluntarily and treated confidentially in accordance with GDPR/Data Privacy regulations. These data will be used solely for diversity monitoring and inclusive selection measures. 

9. Results notification 

Following evaluation by the expert panel, eligible applicants will be ranked according to their final assessment scores. Scholarships will be awarded based on this order of merit, beginning with the highest-ranked candidates. Applicants who meet the evaluation threshold but fall below the cut-off will be placed on a reserve list, ranked by score, and may receive an offer if a selected candidate declines or fails to accept within the stated deadline. Successful applicants must confirm their acceptance of the placement offer within five (5) business days by replying to GEM Global – DIGI-ME Section at digime.mobility@grenoble-em.com. 

10. Redress process 

Applicants who are not satisfied with the evaluation of their application may submit a written appeal within three (3) business days of receiving their result. Appeals will be reviewed by a panel of two GEM Global members and one external member. 

All requests for appeal must be sent to GEM Global – DIGI-ME Section at digime.mobility@grenoble-em.com. 

11. Legal disclaimer 

This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by Grenoble Ecole de Management. The financial support to the selected successful applicants will be provided directly by Grenoble Ecole de Management in its own name and under its own responsibility. Grenoble Ecole de Management’s own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants who will receive the said financial support. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim of increasing the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of Grenoble Ecole de Management. 

Information pursuant to the European General Data Protection Regulation. The personal data of candidates and participants will be processed by Grenoble Ecole de Management for the purposes of DIGI-ME programme. These purposes involve the communication of data to bodies external to Grenoble Ecole de Management (EU Agencies, host institution), as required by current European legislation General Data Protection Regulation no. 2016/679 art. 13. 

For more information: GEM data protection.

beneficiaryAdministration:
1. Aim of the One Semester Exchange Scholarships

The aim of the One Semester Exchange Scholarships (hereinafter referred to as the SCHOLARSHIPS) is to support students in completing their full curriculum through a one semester exchange at the University of Pavia (Italy) or the University of Vaasa (Finland), thereby extending their knowledge and skills in advanced digital technologies (one of the DIGI-ME target areas).

2. DIGI-ME Scholarships 

The SCHOLARSHIPS are granted by the DIGI-ME project. The DIGI-ME project is co-funded by the European Union under Grant Agreement No. 101123009. Up to EUR 21,000 is available to be distributed through targeted scholarships at Grenoble Ecole de Management (hereinafter referred to as GEM). Through this call, up to three (3) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their participation in the DIGI-ME path of a one semester exchange with the University of Pavia, and up to three (3) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their participation in the DIGI-ME path of a one semester exchange with the University of Vaasa. 

3. Financial value 

3.1 Scholarships are provided as a lump sum to support students in paying their tuition fees during the semester exchange. Each selected beneficiary will receive a lump sum for a single mobility action of up to four (4) months, taking place within the period from January 2027 to June 2027, at either the University of Pavia (Italy) or the University of Vaasa (Finland). 

The scholarship comprises a minimum of one component (Item A) and a maximum of two components (Items A and B). 

3.1.1 Fixed component 

Item A: Total contribution towards tuition fees: EUR 3,000 (one-time payment). 

3.1.2 Additional component based on special conditions 

Item B: Additional contribution towards tuition fees for participants with fewer opportunities: EUR 500 (one-time payment). 

Participants with fewer opportunities are defined as students who, prior to the start of the mobility period, meet one or more of the following criteria: 

  1. Are recipients of the French national student grant (CROUS) and belong to one of the four highest grant levels (levels 4, 5, 6, or 7); 
  2. Have a disability with a certified degree of invalidity of at least 50%; 
  3. Hold refugee status and/or benefit from international or subsidiary protection, or are displaced persons; 
  4. Have dependent minor children (students who have given birth to a child during the 2026–2027 academic year, as proven by a birth certificate, up to the child’s first birthday); 
  5. Are engaged in employment (students employed, other than occasionally and not by a family member up to and including the second degree, for a period of at least six months within the 12 months preceding the mobility period, in documented employment, self-employment, or professional activity in the public or private sector); 
  6. Are recognised professional athletes (students who are athletes of national interest must present a certificate from the relevant sports federation); 
  7. Are orphans of at least one parent (a student is considered an orphan if their father and/or mother died before the date of submission of the mobility application. This status is recognised provided that the student: (a) is under 26 years of age at the time of application, and/or (b) was financially dependent on the deceased parent at the time of death or is in a similarly economically dependent situation); 
  8. Are children of victims of terrorism or organised crime. 

Supporting documents for Item B will be requested only from successful applicants. 

4. Payment mechanism 

4.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is paid in two instalments: 

4.1.1 The first instalment, equal to 80% of the total estimated scholarship amount, will be paid within 30 days of signing the Mobility Agreement, provided that the student: 

Has submitted a Learning Agreement duly approved and signed by GEM and the host Higher Education Institution; 

Has correctly entered their bank details in the designated system. 

If any of the above conditions are not met, payment of the first instalment will be made within 30 days of their fulfilment. 

4.1.2 The second instalment, representing the remaining 20%, will be paid at the end of the mobility period, subject to verification of: 

  1. Fulfilment of the administrative and procedural obligations set out in this call; 
  2. Successful completion of the authorised mobility period; 
  3. Achievement of learning outcomes consistent with the Learning Agreement; 
  4. Proper administrative completion of the mobility period, including a duly signed certificate of arrival and a duly signed certificate of departure. 

Failure to comply with any of the above conditions may result in the loss of entitlement to the final payment and may lead to the total or partial recovery of sums already received. 

Acceptance of the mobility period constitutes a formal commitment by the candidate. Consequently, cancellations must be limited to serious and duly documented cases of force majeure. Any cancellation must be communicated in writing to the DIGI-ME Coordinator (digi-me@unipv.it), with GEM Global – DIGI-ME Section (digime.mobility@grenoble-em.com) in copy, adequately justified, and submitted promptly.mailto:digime.mobility@grenoble-em.com Cancellation entails the refund of any financial contributions already received. The reason for cancellation and/or failure to communicate it may be considered when assessing eligibility for future GEM international mobility programmes. 

4.2 Tax treatment 

4.2.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is awarded exclusively to support participation in the one semester exchange programme. The scholarship is intended to contribute to tuition and mobility-related expenses and does not constitute remuneration for employment, services, or research activities. 

4.2.2 Under French tax legislation, grants awarded to support studies and educational mobility are generally not treated as employment income where they are not paid in exchange for work or services. The DIGI-ME scholarship is awarded solely for educational purposes and does not create any employment relationship between GEM and the beneficiary. 

4.2.3 The tax treatment of the scholarship ultimately depends on the individual circumstances of each beneficiary and on the applicable legislation in force at the time of payment. Beneficiaries are solely responsible for determining any personal tax obligations and, where necessary, for making any required declarations to the competent tax authorities. 

4.2.4 GEM does not provide tax advice and accepts no liability for the individual tax treatment of the scholarship. Applicants are encouraged to consult the French tax authorities or a qualified tax adviser if they require guidance regarding their personal tax situation. For more information, please refer to the French tax administration impots.gouv.fr or service-public.fr. 

5. Evaluation process 

Applications must be submitted EXCLUSIVELY through the dedicated form from 18 September 2026 (09:00, Brussels time) to 18 November 2026 (18:00, Brussels time). A complete list of applicants will be compiled, including basic information for statistical and transparency purposes, and may be shared with the European Commission. Applications that pass the eligibility check will undergo an internal evaluation, conducted by a panel of three experts from GEM. For more information on the selection and evaluation process, please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants (Annex 1). The outcome of the call for awarding the DIGI-ME scholarship will be published on the GEM DIGI-ME pagehttps://www.grenoble-em.com/en/faculty-research/funded-projects/future-of-work/digi-me-managing-in-the-age-of-ai/. 

6. Eligibility criteria 

The following applicants are eligible: 

6.1 Students regularly enrolled at GEM at master’s level (M1 or M2). Applicants must be: 

  1. Enrolled for the academic year 2026–2027; 
  2. Full-time students; 
  3. Not on academic leave. 

6.2 Citizens of the European Union (hereinafter referred to as the EU) or of eligible DEP countries (the full list is available here: list-3rd-country-participation_digital_en.pdf). 

6.3 Proficiency in English is a fundamental requirement, as English is the official language of both the Open Call and the master’s programmes. Unless the applicant is a native English speaker, they must provide evidence meeting one of the following minimum requirements: 

  1. TOEFL iBT: 80; 
  2. IELTS Academic / IELTS Indicator: 6.0; 
  3. Cambridge English (Proficiency, Advanced, or Business Higher): Grade A, B, or C; 
  4. Duolingo English Test: 100; 
  5. Bachelor’s degree fully taught in English (official proof required). 

6.4 According to European Union’s rules, it is forbidden to receive double support for the same incurred costs. Hence, the scholarship covered by this call is incompatible with any other EU funding allocated for the same purpose. Applicants must declare that they have not received other European Union funding for the same purpose in the dedicated form. 

7. Required documents 

7.1 Transcripts of records: full higher education transcripts to date, showing passed examinations and related grades. 

7.2 Curriculum vitae (CV): detailed CV outlining academic history, professional experience, skills, and relevant achievements (no photo required; maximum 1 page). 

7.3 Personal statement / motivation letter: statement (maximum 1 page) explaining the applicant’s motivation, interest in the programme, and how their background aligns with the DIGI-ME path of a one semester exchange at the University of Pavia or the University of Vaasa. 

7.4 English language competency: certified evidence of English proficiency meeting the specified minimum scores above. 

7.5 Copy of passport or ID card: copy of a valid passport or identity card. 

7.6 Optional: information on gender, age, and socio-economic status. In the event of equal scores, these factors may be positively considered during evaluation, in line with GEM’s commitment to supporting a diverse student body. 

8. Evaluation criteria and scoring 

8.1 Only eligible candidates will be evaluated. Successful candidates must reach an evaluation threshold of 70%. 

8.2 Applications will be assessed as follows: 

  1. Academic background (65%): based on the weighted average grade and adjusted by the ratio of earned to expected ECTS credits. 
  2. Motivation (25%): reflects the applicant’s commitment to developing advanced digital skills in innovation, international business, and entrepreneurship, as demonstrated in the motivation letter. 
  3. Additional experience (10%): considers academic and non-academic achievements reported in the applicant’s CV. 

8.3 DIGI-ME and GEM are committed to promoting diversity, social and economic equality, and gender balance in all aspects of this open call. As part of our selection process, applicants will have the option to provide information on gender, age, and socio-economic background. In the event of equal scores, priority will be given in the following order: 

  1. Female applicants; 
  2. Applicants from low socio-economic backgrounds; 
  3. Applicants with disabilities; 
  4. Applicants from countries with a low Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI) score; 
  5. Applicants belonging to minority groups. 

8.4 All information provided regarding gender, age, and social background will be collected voluntarily and treated confidentially in accordance with GDPR/Data Privacy regulations. These data will be used solely for diversity monitoring and inclusive selection measures. 

9. Results notification 

Following evaluation by the expert panel, eligible applicants will be ranked according to their final assessment scores. Scholarships will be awarded based on this order of merit, beginning with the highest-ranked candidates. Applicants who meet the evaluation threshold but fall below the cut-off will be placed on a reserve list, ranked by score, and may receive an offer if a selected candidate declines or fails to accept within the stated deadline. Successful applicants must confirm their acceptance of the placement offer within five (5) business days by replying to GEM Global – DIGI-ME Section at digime.mobility@grenoble-em.com. 

10. Redress process 

Applicants who are not satisfied with the evaluation of their application may submit a written appeal within three (3) business days of receiving their result. Appeals will be reviewed by a panel of two GEM Global members and one external member. 

All requests for appeal must be sent to GEM Global – DIGI-ME Section at digime.mobility@grenoble-em.com. 

11. Legal disclaimer 

This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by Grenoble Ecole de Management. The financial support to the selected successful applicants will be provided directly by Grenoble Ecole de Management in its own name and under its own responsibility. Grenoble Ecole de Management’s own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants who will receive the said financial support. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim of increasing the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of Grenoble Ecole de Management. 

Information pursuant to the European General Data Protection Regulation. The personal data of candidates and participants will be processed by Grenoble Ecole de Management for the purposes of DIGI-ME programme. These purposes involve the communication of data to bodies external to Grenoble Ecole de Management (EU Agencies, host institution), as required by current European legislation General Data Protection Regulation no. 2016/679 art. 13. 

For more information: GEM data protection.

beneficiaryAdministration:
1.Summary and purpose of the call

The Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya – Barcelona TECH (hereinafter “UPC”) is soliciting applications for scholarships grants (hereinafter “scholarships”) to support students of the master's degree program “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” (hereinafter “AI4CI Master”) taught at UPC Castelldefels School of Telecommunications and Aerospace Engineering (hereinafter “EETAC”) in Castelldefels, Spain

The UPC- AI4CI scholarships is granted by the “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” (hereinafter “AI4CI project”). The AI4CI project is co-funded by the European Union within the under the Grant Agreement No. 101123524 funded under the topic DIGITAL-2022-SKILLS-03-SPECIALISED-EDU - Specialised education programmes or modules in key capacity areas.

The maximum funding available under this call is €167,500 and may be awarded until the available budget is fully exhausted, provided that this occurs within the overall implementation period of the AI4CI project.

The indicative total number of scholarships to be awarded is approximately 49 ranging from 500 EUR to 4,500 EUR.

The aim of the scholarships is that recipients benefit from AI4CI project's high-quality education in digital areas and to promote equality and excellence in the field of computer science and AI, as well as to increase the accessibility of master's studies developing advanced digital skills and promote the growth of higher-level skills, equality and diversity in computer science.

Converging towards gender equality in ICT fields in EU and the socioeconomic status of the applicant are factors that will be taken into account in the selection process but everyone is welcome to apply regardless their gender and/or socioeconomic situation

This call covers the cohorts 2025-2027 and 2026-2028.

2. Characteristics of support

The scholarship will be awarded to persons (hereinafter referred to as applicants) who are citizens of the European Union, listed EEA countries or of countries associated to Digital Europe Programme and who are currently studying in the AI4CI project master's degree program “AI4CI Master” at “EETAC” in Castelldefels, Spain; as well as those students who have already been pre-admitted to the “AI4CI Master” (2026-2027) and are expected to complete their enrolment in the coming weeks and those who will be admitted to the “AI4CI Master” for the course 2027-2028.

This call offers 4 different support modalities, as described below. Applicants may apply for a combination of different support modalities. However, regardless of the combination of modalities requested, the maximum aggregate scholarship amount that may be awarded to any eligible student is 4.500€.

The maximum amount specified for each modality applies only to that specific modality. Therefore, while different modalities may be combined, the total scholarship amount awarded to any individual student shall not exceed 4.500€. Consequently, no student may receive the maximum amount available under all four modalities simultaneously.

2.1 Reimbursement of tuition fees

Reimbursement of tuition fees includes:                         

  1. The enrollment tuition costs for the full master's program which must be paid before the end of the project.
  2. Administrative and support fees.
  3. The cost of issuance of the official title (if paid before the end of the project)

Each EU beneficiary can be reimbursed up to a maximum of 3.400€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required.

2.2 Contribution to living and transportation expenses

The scholarship supports living and/or transportation expenses. In particular, it covers a monthly allowance of 100 € for a maximum of 6 months between the resolution of the concession and the end of the project.

Each beneficiary can receive a maximum of 600€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required towards reimbursement purposes.

2.3 Contribution to expenses for mobility stays related to the master program

The scholarship supports expenses for in person mobility stays not covered by the Erasmus+ Program related to the AI4CI master program. They must be incurred while the student is enrolled in the program and before the end of the project.

In particular, it supports living, transportation and accommodation expenses related to study collaboration visit to another institution, academic stay at another institution for the master thesis or attendance to courses taught at another university within the framework of the master program.

Each beneficiary can receive a maximum of 500€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required towards reimbursement purposes.

2.4 Other study-related expenses

The scholarship supports expenses for the purchase of hardware and/or software necessary to study; for the acquisition of additional training or information sources, improvement of the necessary competencies and for other study-related expenses. The maximum amount for this modality is up to 1.100€.

3.    Requirements for applicants

1.  Candidates must have been already admitted to the AI4CI master at UPC EETAC or applied to be admitted for the academic year. This means that to be considered for the scholarship, applicants must apply concurrently to the master's program for the cohort 2026-2028 or be already enrolled in the program from the cohort 2025-2027.

2.  Being a full-time degree-seeking student in the AI4CI master's degree program (corresponding to 30 ECTS per semester).

3.  To be an EU citizen or a citizen of one of the listed EEA countries or of one of the countries associated to Digital Europe Programme – provide a copy of the identity document indicating nationality;

4.  For modality 2.2, having monthly rental expenses of at least 200€ or living at a distance of UPC Castelldefels of at least 20 km.

5.For modality 2. 3, the expenses have to be related to the AI4CI master program.

6.  For modality 2.4 a justification letter together with the corresponding quotation(s) dated within the previous 15 days to the application and final related invoices and proof of payments.

4.    Applications

Applications may be submitted according to the following cut-off dates, provided that the maximum available budget has not been exhausted:

  1. 29th September 2026 (23:59h Brussels time).
  2. 5th February 2027 (23:59h Brussels time).
  3. 5th July 2027 (23:59h Brussels time).

The application must be submitted through the UPC Electronic Office filling in the UPC-AI4CI scholarships form. The link is as follows: https://seuelectronica.upc.edu/.

The following documentation has to be attached to the application form:

  1. Cover letter stating the following: presentation of the candidate detailing their academic merits, the motivation and plans, how the received scholarship will be used, how it will contribute to the student’s upskilling in advanced digital skills, and the description of their socioeconomic situation (personal, social, economic, work, etc.) that may be relevant to obtaining the scholarship (mandatory for all modalities);
  2. Documentary evidence of the situations described in the previous point (mandatory for all modalities);
  3. A copy of the identity document showing the date of birth and nationality of the applicant (mandatory for all modalities);
  4. For modality 2.2 also provide documentary evidence of meeting the rental or distance requirements established in point 3.4.
  5. For modality 2.3 also provide information about the mobility stay, letter explaining the purpose and relationship with the master program and budget.
  6. For modality 2.4 also provide information about the hardware or software purpose of study plus a quotation dated within the previous 15 days to the application and the corresponding invoices and proof of payments. The same will apply with regard to the acquisition of additional or information sources towards the improvement of the necessary competencies or other study-related expenses not covered by modalities 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3.

5.     Selection criteria

The selection committee (please refer to clause 7) will evaluate the applications taking into account the academic merit of the candidate as well as the gender and socioeconomic disparities in engineering and computer science.

For modality 2.3, the relationship of the expenses with the AI4CI master program will be checked.

In particular, per each modality, a formula of 8 points based on academic merit and 2 points for gender and socioeconomic situation (1 point if female and 1 point if last year annual income has been less than 21.000€ per year) for a total of 10 points will be assigned to each candidate based on the information candidates provide to the committee. Both the master's program application documents and the additional documentation provided for this scholarship application will be taken into account.

Applications that fulfill the eligibility criteria but are not awarded because of budget limitations will be included in a reserve list (one per each modality). In case one of the awarded candidates can’t accept or refuses the scholarship or loses the financial support, the first candidate in the corresponding reserve list will be automatically re-considered for assessment.

6.    Resolution

Applications for modalities 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 will be continuously assessed.

Within 5 working days after the reception of applications, the selection committee assesses the received applications, their suitability, award points according to the criteria set out in clause 5 and thus rank the applicants. The selection committee selects the best-ranked applicants, but only those who fully meet the Scholarship requirements described in this call.

Scholarship resolutions related to this call will be published through UPC’s Electronic Notice Board (https://seuelectronica.upc.edu/ca/etauler/e-tauler), “e-Tauler”. and will be communicated to all candidates by the selection committee by e-mail on the same day the resolutions are published. All information about awarded scholarships will be published at the UPC-AI4CI Scholarship website.

7.    Payment conditions

Payments related to each modality will be done according to the following schedule, namely:

1. Awarded students coming from the cohort 2025-2027:

  1. 1st Instalment: 21st October 2026.
  2. 2nd Instalment: 29th February 2027.
  3. 2nd Instalment: 30th July 2027.

2. Awarded students coming from the cohort 2026-2028:

  1. 1st Instalment: 29th February 2027.
  2. 2nd Instalment: 30th July 2027. 

8.    Selection committee

The selection committee will be integrated by the members of the Master’s Committee of the AI4CI master program, which currently are:

  1. Prof. Cristina Cervelló-Pastor.
  2. Prof. David Rincón Rivera.
  3. Prof. Carles Gómez Montenegro.

9.    Obligations for applicants

Students who have received Scholarships, within 5 working days upon notification, must present to the selection committee the following documents:

a.      A signed scholarship award agreement, which also specifies the consent to the processing of the student's personal data, for scholarship management and marketing purposes and a series of legal obligations that apply to students receiving the support such as respect of ethics, record-keeping, etc.

b.      Provide the bank details necessary for the transfer of the scholarship.

c. Provide a written declaration, justifying the absence of EU double funding in forms of scholarships.

d.      Document demonstrating that the applicant has successfully completed a minimum of 22.5 ECTS per semester (~75 %).

Students have the right to appeal about the results of the assessment, presenting aspects that they consider inappropriate in their assessment, factual errors in the assessment of the data provided. In the case of an appeal, the following procedure shall apply:

This scholarship is incompatible with any other scholarship, grant, or financial support covering the same eligible expenses in order to avoid multiple funding for the same purposes.

For modality 2.1, scholarships will cover the tuition fees of any semester’s courses until the end of the project as described above.


For modality 2.2, scholarships will cover the allocated monthly amount corresponding to the number of months in which the student is enrolled to the program between the awarding of the scholarship and the end of the project.


For modalities 2.3, scholarships will cover the actual expenses incurred up to the established maximum.

The legal basis for processing is the performance of a task carried out in the public interest (Article 6.1.e of the GDPR) and compliance with legal obligations (Article 6.1.c of the GDPR).


In compliance with the principles of publicity and transparency, and in accordance with the aforementioned regulations and administrative procedure legislation, applicants are informed that the identifying data of candidate (both beneficiaries and those on the waiting list) may be published on the website of the call, on the UPC Transparent portal, and UPC’s Electronic Notice Board (e-Tauler), in accordance with the provisions of Section 6.

They may also lodge a complaint with the Catalan Data Protection Authority (APDCAT) through its website.


In compliance with current regulations, the UPC guarantees that it has adopted the technical and organizational measures necessary to maintain the required level of security, taking into account the nature of the personal data processed.

14. Ethical principles and rules of conduct

In accordance with the provisions of Article 55.2 of Law 19/2014, of December 29, on transparency, access to public information, and good governance, the beneficiaries must align their actions with the UPC Code of Ethics and Good Practices, approved by the Governing Council through Agreement CG/2022/02 of February 22, 2022.

15. Acceptance of the terms and conditions and disclaimer of liability

Participation in this call implies full acceptance of these terms and conditions and the provisions set forth herein. UPC EETAC reserves the right to extend or modify these terms and conditions, and even to cancel or render it void, provided there is a justified cause. Any modifications to the terms and conditions will become effective the day following their publication.


UPC EETAC shall be exempt from any obligation or compensation to the candidates if, due to force majeure, legal mandates, or other criteria of the organization, the call has to be cancelled or suspended.


UPC EETAC shall not be held liable for internet errors or the malfunction of the server where the application form is hosted. The organization reserves the right to exclude from the all any candidate who commits fraud, disrupts the proper and normal course of the call according to the regulations.

beneficiaryAdministration:
1. Purpose of the call

The UPC is opening a call for grants to support students of the Master's Degree in Electronic Engineering (hereinafter, MEE Master's Degree) taught at the UPC's Barcelona School of Telecommunications Engineering (ETSETB).

The aim of these scholarships is to provide financial assistance to MEE students interested in academic training activities in the field of electronics that involve mobility to any of the foreign institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project. The grants cover expenses related to double degree programs and short-term mobility stays at these institutions.


2. Characteristics of the grants

All eligible expenses in this call and described in this document are linked to activities that involve international mobility to one of the foreign institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project.

This call offers 6 different types of grants. The same student can apply for grants corresponding to different blocks, but the maximum amount they can receive in this call will be €10,000, regardless of the limits established in each of the blocks.

The 6 blocks of grants are:


2.1. Refund of tuition and registration fees

This concept includes:

  1. The amount of the credits enrolled for the first time.
  2. The additional fees required, both at the ETSETB and at the institution where the international mobility takes place.
  3. Only semesters that begin before 30/06/2027 are considered.

Each beneficiary may receive a maximum of €3,500.


2.2. Reimbursement of the costs of issuing documentation

This block offers a grant to cover the expenses related to obtaining the documentation required by the host institution, if it is essential to carry out international mobility. Specifically, it includes:

  1. Visa application and issuance.
  2. Life, health, accident, civil liability, etc.
  3. Costs related to the examination and obtaining language accreditation.
  4. Costs derived from the sworn translation of documentation.

Each beneficiary may receive a maximum of €1,000.


2.3. Contribution to specialized training

This block provides support for taking specialization courses related to the GreenChips-EDU project during an international mobility stay at one of the participating foreign institutions

Each beneficiary may receive a maximum of €1,500.


2.4. Contribution to expenses for scientific achievements during the mobility stay

The grant in this block offers support for expenses related to scientific achievements produced during an international mobility to one of the members of the GreenChips-EDU project and linked to the objectives and themes present in the GreenChips-EDU project. Any expense must occur before 30/06/2027. In particular, it covers:

  1. A maximum of €1,000 for expenses related to the publication in full open access of scientific results in first and second quartile journals.
  2. A maximum of €500 for expenses related to the publication in full open access of scientific results in third and fourth quartile journals.
  3. A maximum of €100 for expenses related to the preparation of posters for the presentation of results at a scientific congress.
  4. A maximum of €1,500 for expenses related to registration, travel, accommodation and meals related to attendance at an international scientific congress, CORE B or higher in accordance with the ICORE Conference Portal, for the presentation of an article. This maximum will rise to €2,000 in the event that the congress is considered as CORE A*.


2.5. Contribution to the costs of short-term mobility stays related to the master's degree

This grant offers support for the expenses of short-term face-to-face mobility stays not covered by the Erasmus+ Programme (i.e. less than 2 months and not linked to Blended Intensive Programmes), carried out while the student is enrolled in the MEE and before 30/06/2027.


In particular, it covers up to a maximum of €1,500 for expenses such as transport, accommodation and meals, to international events (e.g. summer campus) or for the completion of the master's thesis in one of the foreign institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project.


2.6. Contribution to the expenses of long-term mobility stays related to the master's degree

This grant offers support for living and/or transport expenses for MEE students who will make an international mobility stay of more than 2 months in one of the foreign institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project. In particular, it covers a monthly grant of €500 linked to the mobility programme, for a maximum of 12 months and always before 30/06/2027. It must be considered that this contribution cannot coincide in time with any other grant for the same concepts and that it is funded by an EU programme (e.g. Erasmus+).

Each beneficiary may receive a maximum of €6,000.


3. Application methods

Students can apply for grants from all six blocks described in section 2, but any application must be made in one of the following two modalities:


3.1. Promotion of the double degree programmes of the MEE.

This modality is intended for students linked to one of the double degree programs within the framework of the MEE, with one of the foreign institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project.

Conditions:

  1. Grants can be applied for in all blocks, except 2.5.
  2. Applications in this modality are given priority over those in any other modality.
  3. The maximum grant that a student can receive, adding up all the concepts, will be €10,000.
  4. The expenses of block 2.1:
  5. They will be covered up to a maximum of 4 consecutive semesters and will include both the credits taken at the ETSETB and the destination of the mobility.
  6. They include the fees for issuing the degrees, both at the UPC and at the international destination, as long as they are paid before 31/07/2027.
  7. The expenses of block 2.6 include the semesters that the student takes the teaching of the double degree program at the ETSETB, that is, those prior to the international mobility taking place.
  8. Documentation proving the expenses incurred will be required.


3.2. Promotion of international mobility in the MEE

This modality is intended for students who have been granted an international mobility place at one of the foreign institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project.

Conditions:

  1. Grants can be applied for in all blocks.
  2. The expenses of block 2.1 will be limited to a maximum of 2 consecutive semesters of mobility.
  3. Documentation proving the expenses incurred will be required.

  1. Candidates must have been admitted to the MEE master's degree taught at the ETSETB or have applied for admission for the 2025/2026 academic year or later. This means that, in order to be considered for the scholarship, applicants must simultaneously submit the application for admission to the Master's degree in Electronic Engineering (MEE) or be already enrolled in the program.
  2. Applicants for modality 3.1 must have been granted a place within the MEE double degree programme at the time of the evaluation of the application, or have the endorsement of the Head of Studies of the MEE and the Deputy Director of International Relations of the ETSETB.
  3. Be an EU citizen or a citizen of Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein or Ukraine.
  4. Be enrolled, at the time they submit the application, in a program linked to the field of electronic engineering or similar, in an HEI located in the EU, Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein or Ukraine.
  5. For the grants of blocks 2.3 and 2.4, the expenses must be directly related to the themes that underpin the GreenChips-EDU project.


5. Submission of applications

Applications can be submitted from the day after the publication of this call and until the available budget is exhausted and, in any case, until June 1, 2027.

The application must be submitted through the UPC's e-Office by filling in the UPC-GREENCHIPS-EDU scholarship form.

The following documentation must be attached to the application form:

  1. Cover letter stating: presentation of the candidate detailing his/her academic merits and the description of his/her situation (personal, social, economic, work, academic performance, etc.) that may be relevant for obtaining the scholarship.
  2. List of grants requested, in accordance with the blocks.
  3. Document stating the average grade of a completed bachelor's degree (or master's degree) that is directly linked to the field of electronic engineering or is directly connected to or has a special relevance to the objectives of the GreenChips-EDU project. It will also be necessary to provide the average grade of the students who have completed that same degree or master's degree in the last 5 years or of as many promotions as available in the event that the degree does not have 5 promotions completed (see section 6.1).
  4. Documentary accreditation of the situations described in the previous point, as well as any of the aforementioned merits.
  5. Accreditation of having a mobility place in one of the destinations admitted by this call, or failing that, a document signed by the Head of Studies of the MEE and the Deputy Director of International Relations that endorses the application. This documentation must indicate the destination of the mobility and the estimated period in which the student will remain abroad.
  6. In the case of applying for grants in block 2.3, write a document justifying the convenience of this training. This document must additionally include, at least, the name and description of the course or activity, its purpose, the entity that teaches it and the location where it takes place.  
  7. For grants in block 2.4, it will be necessary to provide a copy of the publication or poster related to the grant application, the complete reference number of the place of publication, as well as all the documentation required by the UPC, in order to be able to prove the expenses related to the publication.


6. Selection criteria

The evaluation of the applications will be carried out by the selection committee, which will consider the academic merit of the candidate as well as gender and socioeconomic inequalities in the field of electronic engineering.

Each application will be assigned a score based on an evaluation system of 35 points structured in 6 blocks:


6.1. (20 points) Academic performance (r1)

Academic performance will be measured in terms of the average grade (g) of a completed bachelor's degree (or master's degree) that is directly linked to the field of electronic engineering or is directly connected to or has a special relevance to the objectives of the GreenChips-EDU project.

The calculation will be made by comparing the average grade (g) of the applicant with the average grade (gavg) obtained by all students who have completed the same bachelor's or master's degree in the last 5 years. In the case of degrees where there are not 5 completed promotions, as many promotions as available will be taken into account. Results will be normalized according to the minimum (gmin) and maximum (gmax) grades with which the indicated degree or master's degree can be obtained.

Additional considerations:

  1. Applicants are solely responsible for providing the g, gavg, gmax and gmin values. In the event that the selection committee does not have any of this data, the application will receive 0 points in this section.
  2. This information must be certified by the institution where the bachelor's or master's degree was obtained. 


6.2. (5 points) Additional academic merits (r2)

This section assesses academic merits beyond those derived from their academic performance. Specifically:

  1. (+1 point) If the student has completed a bachelor's or master's degree beyond that used for the calculation of r1.
  2. (+1 point) If the student has received a recognition or award for their academic activity. Honors are not included in this consideration.
  3. (+1 point) If the student is the author of a publication or poster in a conference or research journal.
  4. (+1 point) If the student demonstrates training in the field of sustainability or green electronics.
  5. (+1 point) If the student has developed projects related to the field of electronics beyond those required to obtain academic degrees.  

The concepts listed above are considered independently, with r2 being the sum of all those that the student fulfills in accordance with the documentation provided.


6.3. (5 points) Professional experience (r3)

The applicant's work experience in the field of electronic engineering will be valued. Depending on the number of accredited hours, the applicant will receive:

  1. (1 point) Between 100 hours and 500 hours.
  2. (2 points) Between 500 hours and 900 hours.
  3. (3 points) Between 900 hours and 1800 hours.
  4. (4 points) More than 1800 hours.

Applications that prove work experience in the field of sustainability or green electronics will receive an additional point.


6.4. (2 points) Positive gender discrimination (r4)

Two points will be assigned to female applicants, as a mechanism of positive discrimination that seeks to improve the presence of women in the MEE master's degree.


6.5. (2 points) Situation of vulnerability (r5)

The applicant may receive 2 points if they can prove that they are in a situation of socioeconomic vulnerability. This accreditation may be based on other grants already granted and that take this condition into account.


6.6. (1 point) Motivation and alignment with the call (r6)

The student's motivation and the alignment of the application with the objectives of the call will be valued with one point.


Final Thoughts:

  1. The final score (r) of the application is calculated according to the sum of the points obtained in each of the blocks.
  2. With the same score, applications in modality 3.1 will have priority over modality 3.2, as mentioned above.


7. Resolution of applications

Applications will be assessed by a selection committee composed of members of the Academic Committee of the MEE Master's Degree.

The resolutions will be announced electronically to all candidates and information on the scholarships awarded will be published on the GreenChips-EDU project website.

beneficiaryAdministration:
1.  Aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships 

The aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships (hereinafter referred to as SCHOLARSHIPS) is to support students to complete their full curriculum with a triple degree programme at the University of Pavia and Grenoble School of Management to extend their knowledge and skills in advanced digital technologies (one of the DIGI-ME target areas).

2.     DIGI-ME Scholarships 

The SCHOLARSHIPS are granted by the DIGI-ME project. The DIGI-ME project is co-funded by the European Union under grant agreement No. 101123009. Up to 90,000 euros are available to be distributed for the targeted scholarships at the University of Vaasa. Through this call, up to 10 (ten) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their economic participation into the DIGI-ME path of the triple degree programme with the University of Pavia and with Grenoble School of Management. 

3.     Financial value

3.1 Scholarships are provided as a lump sum to cover living and subsistence costs. Each selected beneficiary will receive a lump sum for a single mobility action of 8 to 10 months, depending on the individual Learning Agreement, in the period from January 2027 until May 2027 at the University of Pavia (Italy) and in the period from August 2027 until December 2027 at Grenoble School of Management (France). The scholarship comprises a minimum of two components (items A and B) and a maximum of three components (items A, B, and C).


3.1.1 Fix components:


ITEM A: Monthly contribution: € 500,00;

ITEM B: Travel contribution per destination: € 700,00 (one-time fee);


3.1.2 Additional component based on special conditions: 


ITEM C: Monthly contribution for participants with fewer opportunities: €250,00;

Participants with fewer opportunities are defined as students who, prior to the start of the mobility period, meet one or more of the following criteria:

  1. have a disability with a certified percentage of invalidity of at least 50%; 

2.     hold refugee status and/or benefit from international or subsidiary protection, or are displaced persons; 

3.     have dependent minor children (Students who have given birth to a child during the 2026/27 academic year, as proven by the birth certificate, up to the child's first birthday);

4.     are engaged in employment (Students employed, other than occasionally and not employed by a family member up to and including the second degree, for a period of no less than six months within the 12 months preceding the mobility period, in any documented employment, self-employment, or professional activity, in the public or private sector);

5.     are recognised professional athletes (Students who are athletes of national interest must present a certificate from their relevant sports federation);

6.     are orphans of at least one parent (A student is considered to be an orphan of at least one parent if their father and/or mother have died before the date of submission of the mobility application. This status is recognized provided that the student: (a) has not turned 26 years old at the date of submission of the application, and/or (b) was financially dependent on the deceased parent at the time of death, or is in a similarly economically dependent situation);

7.     are children of victims of terrorism or organised crime. 

Supporting documents for item C will be requested only from successful applicants.

4.     Payment mechanism

4.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is paid in two instalments:

4.1.1 First tranche equal to 80% of the total estimated amount of the scholarship, and paid within 30 days of signing the Mobility Agreement, provided that the student: 

1.     has presented a Learning Agreement duly approved and signed by the University of Vaasa and the host Higher Educational Institution;

2.     has correctly entered the bank details in the Reserved Area.

In the absence of even one of the conditions indicated above, the payment of the first tranche will be made within 30 days of their actual satisfaction.

4.1.2 Second tranche with a balance of 20%, paid at the end of the mobility, subject to verification of compliance with the following conditions: fulfilment of the administrative and procedural obligations set out in this call;

1.     regular completion of the authorised mobility period;

2.     achievement of training results consistent with the Learning Agreement;

3.     correct administrative conclusion of the mobility.

Failure to comply with even one of the above conditions will result in the loss of the right to the balance payment and may lead to the total or partial recovery of the sums already received.

Acceptance of the mobility period constitutes a formal commitment by the candidate. Cancellations must therefore be limited to serious and duly documented cases of force majeure. Any cancellation of the assigned mobility period must be communicated in writing to the DIGI-ME coordinator, digi-me@unipv.it, must be adequately justified, and must be submitted promptly. Cancellation entails the refund of any financial contributions already received. The reason for the cancellation and/or failure to communicate it may be evaluated for the purposes of possible exclusion of the candidate from the subsequent selection process for the University's international mobility programs.


4.2 Tax treatment

4.2.1 The scholarship provided under this call is subject to the applicable Finnish tax legislation. Depending on the nature and purpose of the grant, it may be either tax-exempt or taxable income and may need to be declared in the recipient’s tax return.

4.2.2 Grants or scholarships awarded for studies, academic research, or artistic activities may be tax-exempt. If the grant is paid by a public authority (e.g. the State of Finland, a municipality, or other public bodies), it is generally fully tax-exempt regardless of the amount. If the grant is paid by a private entity, it is tax-exempt only up to the annual limit defined by the State artist grant; any amount exceeding this threshold may be considered taxable income.

4.2.3 Grants are subject to certain mandatory contributions, including the health insurance contribution and the public broadcasting tax. In addition, grant recipients are typically covered by pension insurance under the MYEL system, and the corresponding income may be taken into account when calculating social security contributions.

4.2.4 It should be noted that tax exemption applies only to grants awarded for studies, academic research, or artistic activity. Grants awarded for other purposes are generally considered taxable earned income, regardless of the payer. Recipients are responsible for verifying their individual tax situation and complying with all applicable tax obligations. For more information, please refer to Grants - vero.fi .

5.     Evaluation process  

Submission will be done EXCLUSIVELY via the following dedicated form by 15 October 2026. A complete list of applicants will be compiled, including basic information for statistical and transparency purposes (which will be also shared with the European Commission). Applications that pass the eligibility check will undergo an internal evaluation, conducted by a panel of experts from the University of Vaasa. For more information on the selection and evaluation process please refer to the Guidelines for Applications. The outcome of the call for awarding the DIGI-ME scholarship will be published on the University of Vaasa DIGI-ME project’s website. 

6.     Eligibility criteria

The following persons are eligible for scholarships: 

6.1 Students regularly enrolled [1]in the DIGI-ME project master's degree programmes “Master’s Programme in International Business – Sustainable Global Business (MIB)” and “Master’s Programme in Strategic Business Development (SBD)” at the University of Vaasa:

1. matriculated in the academic year 2026-2027; 

2. full-time students;

3. who have not exceeded the standard duration of the curriculum;

4. not on academic leave.

6.2 Citizens of the European Union (hereinafter referred to as the EU) or DEP Countries (the full list is available here: list-3rd-country-participation_digital_en.pdf )

6.3 Proficiency in English is a fundamental requirement, as it is the official language of both the Open Call and the master's programmes. Unless the applicant is a native English speaker, they must provide a certified score report meeting minimum thresholds: an IELTS Academic score of 6.5, a TOEFL iBT score of 88, or a Cambridge English (C1/C2) score of 180; or having successfully completed a fully-English taught bachelor degree.

6.4 The scholarship covered by this call is INCOMPATIBLE with other EU funds allocated for the same purpose. All applicants must declare they have not received other European Union’s funds in the dedicated form. 

7.     Required Documents 


7.1 Transcripts of Records: Official transcript of records showing grades from the most recently completed studies. If the student has completed studies at a foreign educational institution during the academic year 2025–2026, an official transcript of those study achievements must also be provided in accordance with the regulations and practices of the issuing institution.

7.2 Curriculum Vitae (CV): A detailed CV outlining academic history, professional experience, skills, and relevant achievements (no photo required, max 3 pages).

7.3 Personal Statement/Motivation Letter/Study Plan: A statement (max. 700 words) explaining motivation for applying, interest in the programme, and how applicant’s background aligns with the DIGI-ME path of the triple degree programme at the University of Pavia and Grenoble School of Management. 

7.4 English Language Competency: Certified evidence of English proficiency meeting the specified minimum scores above. 

7.5 Copy of passport or ID card: Copy of a valid passport or identity card.

7.6 Optional: Information on gender, age, and socio-economic status. In case of equal scores, these factors may be positively considered during evaluation, in line with the University of Vaasa commitment to supporting a diverse student body.


8.     Evaluation Criteria and Scoring


8.1 Only eligible candidates will be evaluated. Successful candidates must reach an evaluation threshold of 70%. 

8.2 Applications are assessed based on three components:

  1. Academic background (65%) is assessed based on the weighted average grade, adjusted by the ratio of earned to expected ECTS credits. 

2.     Motivation (25%) reflects applicant’s positive mindset towards advanced digital skills in innovation, international business and entrepreneurship assessed based on the motivation letter.

3.     Additional experience (10%) considers both academic and non-academic achievements as reported in the applicant’s CV.

8.3. DIGI-ME and the University of Vaasa are committed to promoting diversity, social and economic equality, and gender balance in all aspects of this open call. As part of our selection process, applicants will have the option to provide information on gender, age, and socio-economic background. In the case of equal scores assigned to more than one applicant, the selection committee will prioritize female applicants, applicants from low socio-economic backgrounds, applicants experiencing disabilities, applicants from low DESI-countries, and applicants belonging to minority groups, in this order, ensuring a fair and balanced approach to admissions.

Following the experts’ evaluation, all eligible applicants will be ranked according to their final assessment scores. Scholarships will be awarded based on this order of merit, beginning with the highest-ranked candidates. Successful applicants must confirm their acceptance of the formal scholarship offer within five (5) business days by replying to the University of Vaasa Open Call team at digime@uwasa.fi.

Applicants who are not satisfied with the evaluation of their application, may submit a written appeal within five (5) business days of receiving their result. 1.  Aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships 

The aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships (hereinafter referred to as SCHOLARSHIPS) is to support students to complete their full curriculum with a triple degree programme at the University of Pavia and Grenoble School of Management to extend their knowledge and skills in advanced digital technologies (one of the DIGI-ME target areas).

2.     DIGI-ME Scholarships 

The SCHOLARSHIPS are granted by the DIGI-ME project. The DIGI-ME project is co-funded by the European Union under grant agreement No. 101123009. Up to 90,000 euros are available to be distributed for the targeted scholarships at the University of Vaasa. Through this call, up to 10 (ten) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their economic participation into the DIGI-ME path of the triple degree programme with the University of Pavia and with Grenoble School of Management.

3.1 Scholarships are provided as a lump sum to cover living and subsistence costs. The scholarship comprises a minimum of two components (items A and B) and a maximum of three components (items A, B, and C).


3.1.1 Fix components:


ITEM A: Monthly contribution: € 500,00;

ITEM B: Travel contribution per destination: € 700,00 (one-time fee);


3.1.2 Additional component based on special conditions: 


ITEM C: Monthly contribution for participants with fewer opportunities: €250,00;

Participants with fewer opportunities are defined as students who, prior to the start of the mobility period, meet one or more of the following criteria:

  1. have a disability with a certified percentage of invalidity of at least 50%; 

2.     hold refugee status and/or benefit from international or subsidiary protection, or are displaced persons; 

3.     have dependent minor children (Students who have given birth to a child during the 2026/27 academic year, as proven by the birth certificate, up to the child's first birthday);

5.     are recognised professional athletes (Students who are athletes of national interest must present a certificate from their relevant sports federation);

6.     are orphans of at least one parent (A student is considered to be an orphan of at least one parent if their father and/or mother have died before the date of submission of the mobility application. 7.     are children of victims of terrorism or organised crime. 

Supporting documents for item C will be requested only from successful applicants.

4.     Payment mechanism

4.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is paid in two instalments:

4.1.1 First tranche equal to 80% of the total estimated amount of the scholarship, and paid within 30 days of signing the Mobility Agreement, provided that the student:

2.     has correctly entered the bank details in the Reserved Area.

In the absence of even one of the conditions indicated above, the payment of the first tranche will be made within 30 days of their actual satisfaction.

1.     regular completion of the authorised mobility period;

2.     achievement of training results consistent with the Learning Agreement;

NTNU Open Call 2 Offer  

The DigiWind NTNU Open Call 2 presents a valuable opportunity for students aspiring to advance their digital skills through international placement in fields related to the digitalisation of wind and energy systems. 

Through this call, up to fifteen (15) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their exchange stay in Norway during either Spring or Autumn Semester of 2027. 

  1. Award type: Scholarships are provided as stipend to cover living and subsistence costs during the 6-months-exchange period. 
  2. Financial value: Each selected beneficiary will receive a stipend of EUR 6,940. 
  3. Tuition fees: Exchange students from NTNU’s partner universities are exempt from tuition fees in accordance with NTNU Regulations.  
  4. Welfare fee: All students are required to pay a mandatory welfare fee of approximately 70 EUR per semester, which must be covered personally by the applicant. This one-time payment is due by February 1st for Spring semester and September 1st for Autumn semester, and detailed instructions regarding the payment process will be provided by the NTNU International Office as part of the formal admission and enrolment procedure. 
  5. Payment mechanism: Stipends may be distributed via cash cards provided by NTNU’s Unit for International Relations for use within Norway. Disbursement is subject to signing the mobility agreement, confirmation of enrolment, and compliance with all eligibility and reporting requirements outlined in the Open Call. 
  6. Call interdependency: Autumn 2027 scholarships will be funded from the remaining funds after Spring 2027 cut-off, which makes it dependant on the number of candidates successful for the Spring 2027 call.  

Applicants profile 

DigiWind scholarships are available for students undertaking a 6-month study period at NTNU and enrolling in courses within the following eligible M.Sc. programmes: M.Sc. Electric Power Engineering and M.Sc. Marine Technology. 

Applicants must be final year students or hold one of the following degrees obtained at an internationally recognised university or higher education institution: 

  1. Bachelor of Science in Engineering (B.Sc. Eng.). 
  2. Bachelor of Engineering (B.Eng.). 
  3. Bachelor of Natural Science (B.Sc.). 

Applicants must have a background within a relevant field of engineering to meet the prerequisites of the M.Sc. Electric Power Engineering or M.Sc. Marine Technology courses. 

Eligible candidates must be passport holders from EU/EEA countries, or Digital Europe Programme (DEP) associated countries and demonstrate their active student status through an official Certificate of Enrolment for the current academic year in a NTNU partner university.  

Proficiency in English is a fundamental requirement, as it is the official language of both the Open Call and the master's programme. Unless the applicant is a native speaker, they must provide a certified score report meeting minimum thresholds: an IELTS Academic score of 6.5, a TOEFL iBT score of 88, or a Cambridge English (C1/C2) score of 180.  

Candidates are expected to be organized and detail-oriented, ensuring that all necessary documentation is submitted via the F6S platform for the Spring semester by the November 2nd, 2026, or for the Autumn semester by the 1 March 2027 deadline. 

Beyond technical qualifications, successful applicants will reflect DigiWind and NTNU’s core commitment to diversity, social equality, and gender balance. We particularly encourage applications from women and individuals from economically disadvantaged or diverse demographic backgrounds who seek to contribute to the wind energy field.  

Evaluation process  

Submission will be done EXCLUSIVELY via F6S platform Spring 2027 or Autumn 2027. Students are allowed to apply to only one of the semesters (either Spring 2027 or Autumn 2027).  

A complete list of applicants will be compiled, including basic information for statistical and transparency purposes (which will be also shared with the European Commission). 

Applications that pass the eligibility check will undergo an internal evaluation, conducted by a panel of experts from NTNU. For more information on the selection and evaluation process please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants.  

Results notification 

Following the expert’s evaluation, all eligible applicants will be ranked according to their final assessment scores. Scholarships will be awarded based on this order of merit, beginning with the highest-ranked candidates. 

Evaluation results will be compiled into an Evaluation Summary Report. Applicants will be notified of the results via email, as follows: 

  1. For Accepted Applicants: 
  2. An Evaluation Summary Report. 
  3. An invitation to proceed to the enrolment phase and following steps. 
  4. For Rejected Applicants: 
  5. An Evaluation Summary Report for those who passed the eligibility check and underwent internal evaluation phase. 
  6. A rejection letter to ineligible applications. 

Successful applicants must confirm their acceptance of the formal scholarship offer within five (5) business days by replying to the DigiWind NTNU Open Call team at ntnu-opencall@digiwind.org.  

For more details, please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants. 

Redress process 

Applicants who are not satisfied with the evaluation of their application, may submit a written appeal within three (3) business days of receiving their result. Appeals will be reviewed by a panel, chaired by the NTNU DigiWind representative, the Project Officer and one external member.  

Appeals are typically not allowed for disagreements with the academic judgment (score) or if the decision was based on the applicants misunderstanding of the application instructions. Valid grounds for appealing scholarships offer decision generally focus on errors in the assessment process or claims of discrimination. 

All requests for appeal must be sent to the DigiWind NTNU Open Call team at ntnu-opencall@digiwind.org
