The DigiWind Gdańsk Tech Open Call #1 presents an award opportunity for top-performing master's students to accelerate their expertise in the digitalisation of wind and energy systems. 

Funding and Awards 

  1. Gdańsk Tech Open Call #1: For students admitted to the first year of study in the winter and summer semesters of the 2025/26 academic year.   
  2. Number of Scholarships: Thirteen (13) scholarships are available under this first call.   
  3. Award type: Merit-based academic excellence scholarship funded through the Digital Europe Programme and the University's Scholarship Fund.   
  4. Financial value: Each selected beneficiary will receive a one-time lump-sum payment of EUR 5,000.   
  5. Currency conversion: The scholarship will be disbursed in Polish Zloty (PLN), calculated based on the average exchange rate of the National Bank of Poland (NBP) on the day of the transfer.   
  6. Disbursement: The single payment will be disbursed in December 2026 following the announcement of call results and completion of all university administrative formalities. 

Applicants profile 

DigiWind scholarships are available exclusively for students who are already actively enrolled in the M.Sc. in Smart Renewable Energy Engineering programme developed at Gdańsk University of Technology within the DigiWind project framework.  

To be considered eligible, candidates must meet the following baseline profiles: 

  1. Academic milestones: Scholarships may be awarded to students after completion of their second semester (for those admitted in the winter semester) or after completion of their first semester (for those admitted in the summer semester). 
  2. Nationality: Eligible candidates must be passport holders from EU Member States, EFTA/EEA countries, or designated Digital Europe Programme (DEP) associated countries (including Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Serbia, Turkey, and Ukraine). 
  3. Active academic status: Active student status must be validated through an official GPA transcript for the 2025/26 academic year. 

Beyond technical qualifications, the university provides objective accessibility and support to students in difficult financial or health-related situations in accordance with Articles 86 and 95 of the Polish Law on Higher Education and Science. In complete compliance with national legislation (Articles 69(2) and 70(3)), awards are allocated strictly on an objective, merit-based framework. 

Evaluation Process 

Submission will be conducted EXCLUSIVELY via the F6S platform. A complete list of applicants will be compiled, including basic information for statistical and transparency purposes, which will also be shared with the European Commission.   

Applications that pass the administrative eligibility check will undergo an evaluation conducted by a specialised selection Committee officially appointed by the Rector of Gdańsk Tech. The ranking list will be created based on 100% of the GPA from the most recently completed required semester.  

In the case of identical GPA scores among candidates, the ranking order within the tie will be determined based on additional academic or scientific achievements (such as participation in research projects, publications, conference presentations, or scientific club activities) provided in the applicant's optional achievements portfolio.  

For more information, please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants. 

Results Notification 

Following the Committee's evaluation, all eligible applicants will be ranked according to their final assessment scores. Scholarships will be awarded based on this order of merit, beginning with the highest-ranked candidates, up to the 13 available slots.  

The Committee will present the finalized ranking list after the call to the Rector. The final decision on awarding the scholarship rests with the Rector. Applicants will be notified of the results via email on 16 November 2026, as follows:  

  1. For Accepted Applicants: 
  2. An Evaluation Summary Report 
  3. An invitation to proceed to the scholarship agreement signing phase. 
  4. For Reserved or Rejected Applicants: 
  5. A notification of status for those who passed the eligibility check but fell below the 13-beneficiary cut-off, placing them on the reserve list.  
  6. A formal rejection notice for ineligible applications. 

Successful applicants must confirm their acceptance of the formal scholarship offer within five (5) business days of receiving the notification. In the event of resignation or failure to meet the payment conditions, the scholarship offer may be reallocated to the next eligible candidate on the ranking list.   

Redress Process 

Applicants who are not satisfied with the formal procedure or evaluation of their application may submit a written appeal within three (3) business days of receiving their result. Appeals will be reviewed by a specialised panel in compliance with university protocols and chaired by the designated project authorities.  

Appeals are strictly disallowed for disagreements with pure academic judgment or if the decision was based on the applicant's failure to provide mandatory documentation.  

Valid grounds for appealing a scholarship decision focus exclusively on administrative errors in the assessment process or explicit procedural non-compliance. All requests for appeal must be sent to the official DigiWind Gdańsk Tech Open Call team at pg-opencall@digiwind.org

beneficiaryAdministration:
1. Aim, Project, Background and Objective

The AI4CI project, co-funded by the European Union under Grant Agreement No. 101123524, provides financial support to students enrolled in the continuing education master’s programme “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” at Ulm University (UUlm), Germany.

The objective of this call is to increase accessibility to advanced digital skills education, support up- and reskilling of professionals, and promote diversity and inclusion in computer science education.

Within this call, up to 80 fee waivers (with a total amount of max. 80.000 EUR), for individual modules in winter term 2026-2027 (October 2026-March 2027) will be awarded.

A fee waiver covers 80 % of the tuition fee of a module in the AI4CI programme. The module fees range from 585 to 1800 Euros. depending on module size in ECTS and specific characteristics of modules (e.g. inclusion of lab times or high amount of tutoring). Fee waivers therefore range between 468 and 1440 Euros.

Fee waivers apply only to modules taken in the semester for which the waiver is granted.

Applicants may apply for fee waivers for multiple modules, provided they are enrolled in these modules.

2. Eligibility

Applicants must fulfil all the following criteria:

1.   Be a citizen of an EU Member State, an EEA country, or a country associated with the Digital Europe Programme (https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/digital/guidance/list-3rd-country-participation_digital_en.pdf),

2.     Be admitted and enrolled in the master’s programme Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries at Ulm University.

3.     Be registered as a student of the programme in winter semester 2026/2027.

4.     Apply only for modules that

a.  are part of the AI4CI curriculum and

b.     can still be credited toward the final grade and degree.

5.     A fee waiver may be granted only once per module per student.

3. Scope of the Support

  1.       A maximum of 80 module fee waivers will be awarded in this call.
  2.       Each fee waiver reduces the tuition fee of the respective module by 80 %.
  3.       Fee waivers apply only to the semester in which the module is taken.

Students may receive multiple fee waivers, provided they apply for different modules and ranking positions allow it.

4. Application Procedure

4.1 Call Announcement

By 1 October, all admitted students will receive information about:

  1.       the availability of fee waivers,
  2.       the eligibility requirements,
  3.       the application procedure,
  4.       and the application deadline.

4.2 Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by 1 December 2026.

Applicants must submit:

  1.       a completed application form indicating
  2. other modules they will attend in winter semester 2026-2027, and
  3. other modules for which a fee waiver is requested.
  4.       proof of nationality.
  5.       consent allowing the programme administration to access relevant student data in the HIS student administration system and the App4Master admission system.

Applicants may additionally submit supporting documentation relevant to diversity criteria described in Section 7.

5. Evaluation Procedure

Applications will be evaluated by the Study Programme Committee of the AI4CI programme at Ulm University and the corresponding talent scouting team.

The evaluation will take place within 10 working days after the application deadline.

Each module application is evaluated independently.

Applications will be ranked according to the evaluation criteria defined in Section 6 and the tie-breaking and diversity considerations criteria in section 7.

The highest-ranked module applications will receive a fee waiver.

All remaining eligible applications will be placed on a reserve list.

Applicants will be informed about the outcome within five working days after the evaluation.

6. Evaluation Criteria

The fee waiver scheme supports up- and reskilling in advanced AI competencies.

Applications are evaluated based on the curriculum category of the module.

Points are assigned as follows:

Module Area

Points

A2 Mandatory Area – Artificial Intelligence

3

B1 Systems and Networks

2

B2 Automatics and Robotics

2

B3 Processes and Data Management

2

B4 Free Elective Module

1

All module areas are defined in the Subject-Specific Study and Examination Regulations of the AI4CI programme (10 June 2025) and its additional documents.

The maximum score per module application is 3 points.

7. Tie-Breaking and Diversity Considerations

If multiple applications receive the same score, the following criteria will be applied sequentially to determine priority:

  1. Women and gender minorities
  2. Applicants with disabilities
  3. Applicants with family responsibilities or caregiving duties

Supporting documentation may be provided during the application process.

If applications remain tied after applying the above criteria, the final ranking will be determined by random draw conducted by the study programme committee and the talent scouting team.

8. Award and Implementation of the Fee Waiver

Students selected for a fee waiver will receive an updated tuition fee notice reflecting the 80 % reduction for the respective module.

Receiving a fee waiver does not prevent students from applying for other scholarships, unless the conditions of those programmes prohibit it.

However, double funding from EU sources for the same purpose is not permitted.

If a student receives additional funding, the student must provide a written declaration confirming the absence of EU double funding.

If double funding is identified, the fee waiver may be reduced or withdrawn.

9. Appeals

Applicants may submit an appeal only in cases of procedural errors or factual inaccuracies in the evaluation.

Appeals must:

  1. be submitted in writing within five working days after notification of the results;
  2. clearly indicate the alleged procedural error or incorrect data.

The study programme committee will review the appeal and provide a decision within 10 working days.

10. Termination of the Fee Waiver

The fee waiver may be withdrawn if the student:

  1. withdraws from the programme,
  2. takes academic leave,
  3. transfers to another study programme,
  4. or violates academic integrity or ethical standards.

Students may voluntarily withdraw from the fee waiver by submitting a written request.

Unused funding may be reallocated in a future fee waiver call within the AI4CI project.

11. Publication of Results

The final list of fee waiver recipients will be published no later than 15 December 2026.

Personal data will be processed and published in accordance with applicable data protection regulations.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Article 2

Eligibility Criteria


Students enrolled in DIGISOC are eligible to apply for a scholarship only if they meet all of the following criteria:


1.  DIGISOC Students with EU Citizenship or Citizenship from one of the DEP Associates Countries

2.  Students who are enrolled in the second year of the DIGISOC programme for academic year 2026/2027.

3.  DIGISOC Students who have received at least 60 credits for DIGISOC programme courses and completed all courses in which they were enrolled.



Article 3

Application process and period for the academic year 2026/2027


The deadline to submit the applications for the DIGISOC scholarship is 14th December 2026 at 23.59 pm (CET – Central Europe Time).

Applicants are required to upload the necessary documents as listed below on the DIGISOC OpenOlat platform at the following link: 


https://lms.uibk.ac.at/auth/RepositoryEntry/5831590270/CourseNode/113899331829124


Applicants are required to upload the following materials in a single folder labeled with the applicant name:

1)    The signed Application Letter (Annex 1);

2)    The matriculation number at the University which is issuing this call;

3)    The supporting documentation for all eligibility criteria.

The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; all other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is not sufficient, the Evaluation Committee mayrequest additional information or reject the application.


Article 4

Evaluation Committee

A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Dean of the Faculty of Law of the Palacký University, reviews all applications and consists of:

·       One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree awarding universities;

·       At least one DIGISOC student representative;

The Committee is appointed after the deadline for the application submission and terminates the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline.


Article 5

Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure


The joint Evaluation Committee will check eligibility criteria and evaluate each application.

The candidate academic excellence will be evaluated based on the weighted average of grades achieved during academic year 2025/2026 in all DIGISOC courses, calculated and rounded to hundredths (e.g. 28,77) on a 30 points scale according to the DIGISOC grade conversion table. Based on averages, students who have submitted their application will be put in descending order. In case of tie, they will be put on shared place, awarding the higher award.


To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use the following model:


·      the Student with highest average will be awarded a 2000 EUR scholarship.

·      the Student with second highest average will be awarded a 1750 EUR scholarship.

·      the Student with third highest average will receive a 1500 EUR scholarship.

·      All other students with average above 26,99 will receive a scholarship which corresponds to the result of dividing the call's remaining budget by the number of applications fulfilling the award criteria, but not exceeding 1000 EUR per applicant.


The joint Evaluation Committee’s judgement is unquestionable.

The rankings and the exact amount of funding received by each applicant will be published on the DIGISOC website (https://digitalsociety4innovation.eu/costs-and-scholarships/) and the DIGISOC Awarding Universities Websites. This publication has the value of notification.
description:
Article 1

Purpose, amount and duration of the DIGISOC Scholarship


The Palacký University is issuing a Call for Application within the DIGISOC Scholarship Programme, reserved for students enrolled for the Academic Year 2026/2027 in the second year of the Joint Master’s Programme in Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (DIGISOC).

The Call for Application has a total budget of EUR 11.000,00.

The DIGISOC Scolarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the DIGISOC Joint Master’s Programme (JMP) and aims to:

·      Reward students with outstanding academic performance;

·      Promote excellence in higher education;

·      Alleviate costs associated with tuition fees, summer schools, short-term mobilities, and living expenses.

The scholarships also function as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic obstacles that hinder participation in international education.

The DIGISOC scholarship is limited to one academic year. The scholarships are paid out in one instalment.

There is no automatic entitlement to scholarships and there is no automatic renewal.

The amount of the scholarship can reach a maximum of EUR 2.000,00 each (gross percipient) per academic year and applicant.

The exact amount of the Scholarship assigned to each applicant is based on the grade average based on criteria set in Article 5 – Award Criteria.

The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; all other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is not sufficient, the Evaluation Committee mayrequest additional information or reject the application.


Article 4

Evaluation Committee

A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Dean of the Faculty of Law of the Palacký University, reviews all applications and consists of:

·       One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree awarding universities;

·       At least one DIGISOC student representative;

The Committee is appointed after the deadline for the application submission and terminates the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline.


Article 5

Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure


The joint Evaluation Committee will check eligibility criteria and evaluate each application.

The candidate academic excellence will be evaluated based on the weighted average of grades achieved during academic year 2025/2026 in all DIGISOC courses, calculated and rounded to hundredths (e.g. 28,77) on a 30 points scale according to the DIGISOC grade conversion table. Based on averages, students who have submitted their application will be put in descending order. In case of tie, they will be put on shared place, awarding the higher award.


To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use the following model:


·      the Student with highest average will be awarded a 2000 EUR scholarship.

·      the Student with second highest average will be awarded a 1750 EUR scholarship.

·      the Student with third highest average will receive a 1500 EUR scholarship.

·      All other students with average above 26,99 will receive a scholarship which corresponds to the result of dividing the call's remaining budget by the number of applications fulfilling the award criteria, but not exceeding 1000 EUR per applicant.


The joint Evaluation Committee’s judgement is unquestionable.

The rankings and the exact amount of funding received by each applicant will be published on the DIGISOC website (https://digitalsociety4innovation.eu/costs-and-scholarships/) and the DIGISOC Awarding Universities Websites. This publication has the value of notification.

Eligibility Criteria

Students enrolled in DIGISOC for the second year are eligible to apply for a scholarship if they meet one or more of the following criteria:

1. Students with certified disabilities

Students with certified disabilities can apply for a DIGISOC scholarship. In the context of this call, and following Article 1 of the European Disability Policy, students with disabilities are considered students who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which, in interaction with various barriers, may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. Applicants must provide certified medical documentation or proof of a national disability status.

2. Migrants or refugees

Students who are migrants or refugees can apply for funding based on their status. Required proof may include an asylum decision, a residence permit, or confirmation issued by a migration authority.

3. Students with low socio-economic family conditions

Students from families with low socio-economic conditions can apply for funding. Low socio-economic conditions are defined according to the student’s family income. Required proof may include a tax statement, an income certificate, or an official social benefit statement.

4. Students living in remote areas

Students living in a region in the lowest 25% of national population density and/or with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius may apply. Required proof is a residence certificate, which will be assessed against infrastructure data based on national statistics.


Application process and period for the academic year 2026/2027

The deadline to submit applications for the DIGISOC scholarships is 10. December 2026 at 23.59 CET (Central European Time).

Applicants are required to upload the necessary documents listed below on the DIGISOC OpenOlat platform at the following link:

https://lms.uibk.ac.at/auth/RepositoryEntry/5831590270/CourseNode/114518610654144

Applicants are required to upload the following materials in a single folder labelled with the applicant’s name:

·       The signed Application Letter (Annex 1);

·       The applicant’s registration number (Matrikelnummer) at the University of Innsbruck;

·       The supporting documentation for each claimed eligibility criterion, issued by a responsible authority or accredited expert.

·       The Data Protection and Consent Declaration (Annex 2).

The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; documents in other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is insufficient, the Evaluation Committee may request additional information or reject the application.

By submitting the application and signing Annex 1, the applicant expressly confirms that the application has been submitted completely and correctly and that all information and supporting documents are accurate and complete. Incomplete applications may be excluded from the selection procedure.


Evaluation Committee

A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Study Coordinator (Studienbeauftragter) of the Faculty of Economics and Statistics of the University of Innsbruck, reviews all applications and consists of:

·       One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree-awarding universities;

·       At least one student representative from the University of Innsbruck;

·       Disability officer at the University of Innsbruck.

The Committee is appointed after the deadline for application submission and completes the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline.


Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure

The joint Evaluation Committee will evaluate each application and award points based on the following criteria:

1. Students with certified disabilities

Applicants will be awarded points on the basis of the severity and impact of their condition, ranging from 5 points for a comparatively less impactful disability to 10 points for a very serious disability.

2. Migrants or refugees

Applicants will be awarded points as follows: 

a.         10 points for refugee status; 

b.         10 points for migrant status with less than 5 years in the current country of residence; 

c.         5 points for migrant status with 5 or more years in the current country of residence.

3. Low socio-economic family condition

Applicants will be awarded 10 points if their family income falls within the first quartile (Q1), i.e. within the 25% of the population with the lowest incomes in their country of origin. Applicants will be awarded 5 points if their family income falls between the first and second quartile (Q2), i.e. within the range defined by the median income and Q1 in their country of origin. The reference fiscal year is the year preceding the year in which the application is submitted.

4. Remote areas

Applicants will be awarded 5 points for residence in a remote area. An additional 5 points will be awarded if the student’s residence is in a remote area with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius.

All applications will be ranked on the basis of the sum of points obtained across the four criteria. Each application can obtain a maximum of 30 points.

To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use a proportional point-based model:

·       Total funds available are divided by the sum of all points awarded across valid applications;

·       This determines a value per point (EUR/point);

·       Each applicant receives funding according to their own score, up to the maximum of EUR 3,000.00.

The decision of the joint Evaluation Committee is final, subject to the appeal procedure set out in Article 6.

The exact amount of funding and its composition awarded to each applicant will be published via the Learning Management System OpenOLAT. This publication constitutes as notification.

Purpose, amount and duration of the DIGISOC Scholarship

The University of Innsbruck is issuing a Call for Application within the DIGISOC Scholarship Programme, reserved for students enrolled for the Academic Year 2026/2027 in the second year of the Joint Master’s Programme in Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (DIGISOC).

The Call for Application has a total budget of EUR 50.000.

The DIGISOC Scholarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the DIGISOC Joint Master’s Programme (JMP) and aims to:

·       Alleviate costs associated with tuition fees, summer schools, short-term mobilities, and living expenses;

·       Support students from underprivileged or vulnerable backgrounds;

·       Promote diversity, fairness, and gender balance in higher education.

The scholarship also functions as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic obstacles that hinder participation in international education.

The DIGISOC Scholarship is limited to one academic year and is paid out in one instalment. There is no automatic entitlement to a scholarship and no automatic renewal.

The amount of the scholarship can reach a maximum of EUR 3,000.00 gross per academic year and applicant. The exact amount assigned to each applicant is based on the points awarded in the evaluation process (see Article 5 – Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure).

A maximum of 30 points can be awarded to each application. The maximum total funding per student is EUR 6,000.00 over the course of the two-year programme.

For the entire academic year for which the scholarship is awarded, the scholarship holder must not have an employment relationship with the University of Innsbruck. 

Applicants and scholarship holders are solely responsible for clarifying and complying with all tax obligations and any other individual tax consequences arising from receipt of the scholarship. The University of Innsbruck does not provide individual tax advice.

Applicants are notified of decisions within 15 days after the end of the submission period via e-mail. Rejected applications include a short justification.

Applicants who are not awarded a scholarship have the right to appeal. Appeals may be submitted by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at and will be reviewed by the joint Evaluation Committee, including the designated representative responsible for disability, inclusion and/or equal-treatment matters.

Within the mandatory deadline of 5 days from receipt of the scholarship award notice, the applicant must send the declaration of acceptance by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at without reservation and under the conditions of this Call for Application. Failure to do so results in forfeiture of the award.

With the declaration of acceptance, the scholarship holder must also undertake to communicate any change occurring during the academic year that affects information previously declared or eligibility for the scholarship.


Requirements for receiving the scholarship

Before disbursement, the scholarship holder will complete the required scholarship documentation with the University of Innsbruck and must provide:

·       A current enrolment certificate showing the register number;

·       The applicant’s full residential address (street and house number, postal code, city, and country);

·       Bank details for an account held in the scholarship holder’s name, including an IBAN and any further information required to enable a SEPA credit transfer. It must be expressly possible to make the scholarship payment by SEPA transfer to the account provided;

·       A copy of a valid passport or other accepted identification document.

Scholarship holders remain solely responsible for all tax-law clarifications and obligations connected with the scholarship.

The scholarship holder must also confirm that no employment relationship with the University of Innsbruck exists or will exist for the duration of the academic year for which the scholarship is awarded.


Financial and Disbursement Procedures

Scholarships are paid in one instalment per academic year. 

Disbursement is handled by the University of Innsbruck as the DIGISOC degree-awarding university issuing this Call for Application.

Payment will be made by SEPA credit transfer to a current account in the name of the scholarship holder. The account provided must be capable of receiving a SEPA transfer. The scholarship holder is responsible for providing complete and correct bank details and for any bank charges or conversion costs that may arise outside the scope of the SEPA payment.


Renunciation

In the event of withdrawal from the scholarship after acceptance, scholarship holders must give written notice by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at.

In case of transfer to another programme during the 2026/2027 academic year, the scholarship holder will be considered to have renounced the scholarship and must return the full amount of the scholarship.

A scholarship holder who renounces the scholarship is required to return any amounts received, except in duly justified special cases, which will be assessed by the joint Evaluation Committee.


Final provisions

All resources and updates will be made available via the DIGISOC website – Costs and Scholarships page https://digitalsociety4innovation.eu/costs-and-scholarships/

results.content: Round 2: Small Grants for Grassroots Coding Projects as part of EU Code Week

beneficiaryAdministration: A selection committee comprising community stakeholders and representatives from the Code4Europe Consortium will evaluate proposals. Each proposal will be assessed based on four main criteria: presentation (clarity and completeness of the application), design congruity (relevance to EU Code Week priorities, coherence and feasibility of activities, and availability of professional and organisational resources), quality (the educational approach, alignment with core digital and literacy competencies, collaboration with local networks, and potential for replicability), and impact (engagement of diverse stakeholders, inclusion of different participant groups, and specific attention to involving girls and fostering STEM education). The evaluation process will be transparent and objective, with measures in place to avoid any conflicts of interest.
description:
The purpose of this call is to identify and support projects that can foster EU Code Week’s mission to promote coding, computational thinking, and digital skills across Europe.

The aim is to identify projects that can achieve large-scale impact and deliver on key EU Code Week performance indicators within the project implementation period. 

Key tasks: 

  1. Supporting the organisation of a large number of impactful coding, computational thinking, digital skills, and STEM activities; 
  2. Increasing the number of activities registered on the EU Code Week platform; 
  3. Reaching a large number of participants through local, regional, national, or cross-border activities; 
  4. Increasing the participation of girls and young women in coding, digital skills, and STEM education; 
  5. Supporting career-focused events that introduce students to educational and professional opportunities in STEM and digital fields; 
  6. Supporting university visits and other activities that strengthen connections between schools, students, and higher-education institutions; 
  7. Supporting activities and approaches that can be replicated or scaled beyond the project implementation period. 

Priority will be given to projects that can deliver a large number of activities to the EU Code Week platform and participants while maintaining educational quality and demonstrating clear and measurable impact.

description:
Within the framework of the SUSA project, two partners—METU and GNOMON Informatics SA —will offer internships to degree program students. Below is a consolidated explanation of the criteria, procedures, and financial mechanisms that will govern the provision of third-party financial support related to these internships.

For METU, the maximum amount of financial support for each third-party recipient is set at €610 per internship, in accordance with internal standards for internship remuneration and as aligned with the granting authority’s guidelines.

This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by MIDDLE EAST TECHNICAL UNIVERSITY (METU). The financial support to the selected successful applicants will be provided directly by METU in its own name and under its own responsibility. METU’s own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants that will receive the said financial support. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim to increase the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of METU. 

METU’s financial support amount is derived from internal remuneration benchmarks for student internships. 

For both METU and GNOMON, internships must be aligned with the thematic focus of the SUSA project, including but not limited to: 

  1. Digital health and healthcare innovation 
  2. Health data management and interoperability 
  3. Artificial intelligence applications in healthcare 
  4. Advanced digital skills development and practical application of SUSA educational content 

Internship positions will be open to students enrolled in degree programs, with a focus on engineering and health-related disciplines that are relevant to the SUSA learning objectives. 

To align with academic cycles and optimize visibility, seven internship calls are planned throughout the project. Announcement will be published in June 2025 before the start of the Fall 2025-2026 academic semester with the following cutoff dates:

furtherInformation:
INTERNSHIP OPPORTUNITY


TITLE OF INTERNSHIP: Hands-On AI & Data Science Internships

LOCATION: 

Remote (Virtual) or On-Site at Informatics Institute of Middle East Technical University

DURATION: 4 weeks

ELIGIBLE CANDIDATES: Biology, Molecular Biology and Genetics, Engineering, and Biomedical - Bioinformatics Students (BSc/MSc)

OVERVIEW

The Informatics Institute provides a unique research and learning environment across the interdisciplinary fields of medical informatics, bioinformatics, data informatics, and information systems.

We're offering exciting internship opportunities for students passionate about Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science, and Digital Health Technologies. This hands-on experience will deeply immerse you in: 

  1. Nextflow Pipelines: You'll work with NextFlow computational workflows, seamlessly integrated with container technologies like Docker and Singularity, for critical analyses such as differential gene expression and differential ChIP-seq. 
  2. SigProfiler Suite: You'll gain expertise with the powerful SigProfiler tools specialized in cancer genomics, including SigProfilerMatrixGenerator, SigProfilerSimulator, SigProfilerExtractor, SigProfilerAssignment, and SigProfilerTopography. 

This experience will transform your theoretical knowledge into practical, in-demand skills, preparing you for a successful career in data-driven scientific fields. 


DELIVERY MODE & WORK ENVIRONMENT 

  1. Virtual Internships: A cost-effective alternative allowing students to work remotely. 
  2. On-Site Internships: Available in the classroom at the Informatics Institute for students who prefer in-person collaboration. 
  3. Hybrid Approach: Combining remote and on-site work for flexibility. 

Interns will work in small interdisciplinary teams under the guidance of mentors, engaging in collaborative research and development. 

 

WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON 

  1. Building Robust Nextflow Pipelines: Developing and optimizing Nextflow computational workflows that leverage Docker and Singularity container technologies. These pipelines will be crucial for performing advanced analyses like differential gene expression and differential ChIP-seq. 
  2. Mastering the SigProfiler Suite: Becoming proficient with a suite of powerful SigProfiler tools, specifically SigProfilerMatrixGenerator, SigProfilerSimulator, SigProfilerExtractor, SigProfilerAssignment, and SigProfilerTopography. 

TECHNOLOGIES YOU’LL USE  

  1. Python, R 
  2. Nextflow 
  3. SigProfiler suite of tools 

WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU  

  1. Curiosity and willingness to learn 
  2. Python programming knowledge 
  3. Interest in computational biology and bioinformatics 
  4. Teamwork skills 

 


LEARNING OUTCOMES 

Upon completion, interns will: 

✅ Design & Implement Nextflow Pipelines. 

✅ Master Containerization Technologies. 

✅ Ensure Workflow Reproducibility. 

✅ Manage Large-Scale Data. 

✅ Mastering the powerful SigProfiler tools for cancer genomics analysis. 

 

ASSESSMENT & CERTIFICATION 

  1. Completion of assigned tasks and active participation in projects. 
  2. Development of a mini research report or technical presentation at the end of the internship. 
  3. Issuance of an Internship Certificate by the Informatics Institute of Middle East Technical University. 

 

 

APPLICATION PROCESS 

Interested students should submit: 

📌 A short CV highlighting relevant skills and background. 

📌 A brief motivation letter (max. 1 page) explaining their interest in the internship. 

📩 Applications should be sent to: [burcako@metu.edu.tr] with the subject: 

“SUSA Internship Application – [Your Name]” 

For more details, visit contact [burcako@metu.edu.tr].  

This internship offers a unique opportunity to fill the gap between foundational academic knowledge and the practical, industry-ready skills required to excel in the rapidly evolving landscape of data-driven digital health. 

Financial support will be available to facilitate student mobility. SUSA students will have access to internship opportunities offered by both consortium members and affiliated ecosystem partners. The selection criteria for these internships will be developed collaboratively through a co-design process and will incorporate Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) principles, with particular attention to gender and the socio-economic background of applicants.

Student exchanges between Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) will be further supported through a structured and mentored Erasmus+ mobility initiative. To assist students in planning their mobility paths, joint SUSA learning activities will be organized. Additionally, the SUSA Virtual Academy will host a dedicated matchmaking platform, enabling students and teachers to explore internship opportunities and allowing healthcare ecosystem stakeholders to promote openings and connect with emerging talent.

furtherInformation:
INTERNSHIP OPPORTUNITY

Empowering Future Healthcare and Engineering Professionals through Digital Health Innovation

TITLE OF INTERNSHIP:

Digital Health & AI Internships at Gnomon Informatics

LOCATION:

Remote (Virtual) or On-Site at Gnomon Informatics SA Offices

DURATION: 

4 months  

ELIGIBLE CANDIDATES: 

Medical, Engineering and Biomedical - Bioinformatics Students (BSc/MSc) 

OVERVIEW 

Gnomon Informatics SA, a leading informatics company specializing in digital health solutions, is offering internship opportunities for students interested in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science, and Digital Health Technologies. This internship provides hands-on experience with eHealthPass, a certified patient-centered platform for remote patient monitoring, which includes a mobile app for patients and a web application for healthcare professionals. eHealthPass is a solution for remote care, virtual care and hospital at home, as well as communication and patient empowerment tool, putting patient in the middle and allowing patient to become stakeholder in own care instead of being mere subject of care. Behind eHealthPass there is also the eHealthPass.CDR, a platform providing and enabling HIE (Health Information Exchange) – complete lifecycle management of structured and unstructured clinical documents and clinical data, and their secure sharing/exchange.  

Interns will contribute to AI development, data quality enhancement, and predictive analytics in healthcare, gaining invaluable experience in a multidisciplinary setting. 

 

INTERNSHIP TRACKS 

1. Medical Students – AI and Digital Health Applications 

  1. Assisting in training AI models by feeding them with structured and unstructured medical data. 
  2. Understanding and improving AI-assisted decision support tools for clinical applications. 
  3. Exploring ways to generate customized outcomes and predictions for individual patients. 
  4. Medical file structures and content (questionnaires, educational and other materials) 
  5. Usability of the product 

2. Engineering & Data Science Students – Data & AI Optimization 

  1. Contributing to data quality assessment and enhancing data mesh architecture. 
  2. Developing and testing AI tools for predictive analytics and patient monitoring. 
  3. Exploring interoperability challenges in digital health using HL7 FHIR and other HL7 standards (HL7v2 messages, HL7 CDA). 
  4. Assisting in data visualization techniques to support decision-making for healthcare providers (UX/UI for HealthTech) 

3. Bioinformatics/ Biomedical Students – Clinical Data  

  1. Clinical data model and governance 
  2. Terminology management 
  3. GDPR & EHDS issues 
  4. eHealthPass use cases validation & scenarios 

 

DELIVERY MODE & WORK ENVIRONMENT 

  1. Virtual Internships: A cost-effective alternative allowing students to work remotely while accessing Gnomon’s digital infrastructure. 
  2. On-Site Internships: Available at our company headquarters for students who prefer in-person collaboration. 
  3. Hybrid Approach: Combining remote and on-site work for flexibility. 

Interns will work in small interdisciplinary teams under the guidance of mentors and domain experts, engaging in collaborative research and development. 

WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON 

  1. Healthcare Interoperability: Learn and apply standards like FHIR, HL7, and IHE XDS. 
  2. Artificial Intelligence: Participate in AI-powered solutions for clinical decision support, health record processing, and document classification. 
  3. Software Development: Collaborate in real projects, using Java, Spring Boot, Python, APIs, and cloud platforms (Azure, AWS). 
  4. Medical Data Processing: Work with EHR systems, patient summaries, and secure document exchanges 
  5. R&D Projects: Contribute to European Research Projects and pilot implementations in real healthcare settings. 

TECHNOLOGIES YOU’LL USE  

  1. Java/ Spring Boot/ Python 
  2. FHIR/ HL7/ IHE 
  3. Azure/ AWS/ Docker/ Kubernetes 
  4. AI Models/ Prompt Engineering/ LLMs  

WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU   

  1. Curiosity and willingness to learn 
  2. Basic programming knowledge (preferably Jana or Python) 
  3. Interest in healthcare or AI 
  4. Teamwork skills  

 

LEARNING OUTCOMES 

Upon completion, interns will: 

✅ Gain practical experience in digital health platforms and AI integration. 

✅ Understand data governance, privacy regulations (GDPR), and interoperability. 

✅ Develop hands-on skills in data science, machine learning, and healthcare informatics. 

✅ Enhance problem-solving and critical thinking abilities in a real-world healthcare environment. 

 

ASSESSMENT & CERTIFICATION 

  1. Completion of assigned tasks and active participation in projects. 
  2. Development of a mini research report or technical presentation at the end of the internship. 
  3. Issuance of an Internship Certificate by Gnomon Informatics SA, potentially co-branded with academic institutions. 

 

APPLICATION PROCESS 

Interested students should submit: 

📌 A short CV highlighting relevant skills and background. 

📌 A brief motivation letter (max. 1 page) explaining their interest in the internship and preferred track (Medical or Engineering). 

📩 Applications should be sent to: a.karabatea@gnomon.com.gr with the subject: 

“Digital Health Internship Application – [Your Name]” 

For more details, visit contact a.karabatea@gnomon.com.gr . 

This internship offers a unique opportunity to fill the gap between foundational academic knowledge and the practical, industry-ready skills required to excel in the rapidly evolving landscape of data-driven digital health. 

Financial support will be available to facilitate student mobility. SUSA students will have access to internship opportunities offered by both consortium members and affiliated ecosystem partners. The selection criteria for these internships will be developed collaboratively through a co-design process and will incorporate Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) principles, with particular attention to gender and the socio-economic background of applicants.

To assist students in planning their mobility paths, joint SUSA learning activities will be organized. Additionally, the SUSA Virtual Academy will host a dedicated matchmaking platform, enabling students and teachers to explore internship opportunities and allowing healthcare ecosystem stakeholders to promote openings and connect with emerging talent.

- Any documentation supporting disadvantaged background and/or priority categories (where applicable),

EUR 5 000 (for both priorities/objectives 1 and 2)

as reported in the indicative cost breakdown (see above). The Selection Committee may cap specific cost items if considered excessive or not in line with typical market prices for the location and period.

For both priorities/objectives, eligible expenses are those realised after the date of submission of the respective application.

The priority/objective 1 scheme reimburses up to 50% of total eligible costs, within the 5 000 EUR cap, so that the minimum number of supported beneficiaries with available resources (equally distributed across two yearly editions of this Call) will be at least 156.

The priority/objective 2 scheme reimburses an equivalent amount to the one perceived by the intern, within the 5 000 EUR cap, so that the minimum number of supported beneficiaries with available resources (equally distributed across two yearly editions of this Call) will be at least 234.

results.content: Phortify Internship (Traineeship) Grants - Pilot Call

beneficiaryAdministration:
Phortify Internship (Traineeship) Grants

Under this call, Phortify internships refer to short-term, practice-oriented placements, as foreseen in the Phortify Grant Agreement. They are learning-based activities and do not constitute employment.

The Phortify Internship Grants support both students enrolled in Phortify Master’s Degree Programmes and students who are not enrolled in a Phortify Master’s programme, provided that the internship is Phortify-labelled, aligned with the objectives of the Phortify project, and carried out in accordance with the Phortify Grant Agreement.

Participating partners:

Activer Fiber Systems (AFS):

- https://www.afs-jena.de/

ICFO - The Institute of Photonic Sciences:

- https://www.icfo.eu/

Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e):

- Master of Science in Applied Physics

- Master of Science in Electrical Engineering: track (1) Semicon Devices and track (2) Connected World Technologies

Warsaw University of Technology (WUT):

- Master of Science in Mechatronics

- Master of Science In Photonics

Friedrich Schiller University (FSU):

- Master of Science in Photonics

- Master of Science in Quantum Science & Technology


How to apply for funding

Funding opportunities will be advertised through (1) the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, (2) the official Phortify website (https://phortify.eu/my-phortify/) and (3) the official Phortify partner websites.

Applications for Phortify funding must be submitted via the Phortify website. Applicants are required to consult the dedicated MyPhortify page, where all funding opportunities available under this pilot call are listed together with detailed application instructions and links to the relevant local application forms.

Nationality eligibility

  1. Applicants must be nationals of an EU Member State, an associated country, or a country with which the European Union has an ongoing cooperation agreement under the Digital Europe Programme.
  2. Eligible countries include, inter alia, countries participating in Digital Partnerships, Trade and Technology Councils, digital dialogues, or other forms of ongoing international cooperation with the European Commission in the field of digital technologies.

The authoritative list of eligible countries will be published as part of this call and may be updated in accordance with European Commission guidance.

Eligibility

Under this call, Phortify Internship Grants may be awarded to students belonging to one of the following categories:

Category A – Phortify master degree-seeking students

Students who are enrolled in one of the Phortify Master’s Degree Programmes offered by the consortium universities and who undertake a Phortify-related internship during their period of study.

Category B – Phortify non-degree seeking students participating in Phortify student activities

Students who are not enrolled in a Phortify Master’s Degree Programme but who participate in a Phortify-labelled internship, as foreseen under the Phortify Grant Agreement and implemented under the responsibility of a Phortify partner institution.

In all cases, eligible applicants must be students at the time of the internship, and the internship must:

  1. be directly related to the thematic areas and objectives of the Phortify project;
  2. contribute to the academic and professional development of the student;
  3. be carried out during the student’s period of study;
  4. be implemented under the responsibility of a Phortify partner institution.

Applicants must submit the following documentation:

  1. Latest official academic BSc and MSc (if applicable) transcripts
  2. A Phortify-specific motivation letter, describing the applicant’s motivation for applying for Phortify funding and their alignment with the objectives of the Phortify project
  3. A curriculum vitae (CV)

Applications that fail to meet the minimum eligibility requirements or that do not include the required documentation will be declared ineligible and will not be further evaluated.

Evaluation and selection

The predefined evaluation framework applicable to this call is published on the Phortify website as a dedicated evaluation framework document and applies to all partner institutions.

1. Purpose and Scope

This description defines the evaluation framework applied to applications submitted under the Phortify Internship Grants – Pilot Call.

The framework ensures transparency, equal treatment of applicants, consistency across partner institutions, and alignment with the objectives of the Phortify project, including its Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) principles.

2. Evaluation Principles

The evaluation process is based on the following principles:

  1. Transparency and traceability of decisions
  2. Equal and fair treatment of all applicants
  3. Merit-based selection
  4. Consideration of DEI objectives in line with EU guidance

3. Evaluation Process Overview

The evaluation consists of two sequential stages:

  1. Eligibility verification (pass/fail)
  2. Comparative assessment and ranking

4.  Stage 1 – Eligibility Verification

Applications are checked for compliance with all eligibility requirements defined in the call text. Applicants must submit all required supporting documentation, including academic transcripts, a Phortify-specific motivation letter, and a curriculum vitae (CV).

Applications that fail to meet the eligibility requirements or that do not include the required documentation are declared ineligible and are not further evaluated.

5.   Stage 2 – Comparative Assessment

Eligible applications are assessed comparatively using the criteria below. Each criterion is scored independently on a scale from 0 to 5 points.

Evaluation Criteria

  1. Academic Excellence (0/5): Academic performance, relevance of previous studies, and preparedness for the proposed internship.
  2. Motivation and Alignment with Phortify Objectives (0/5): Quality, coherence, and relevance of the motivation letter, including alignment with Phortify’s educational and societal objectives.
  3. Overall Applicant Profile (0/5): Skills, experience, background, and potential contribution to the Phortify community, as reflected in the CV.

Maximum total score: 15 points.

Ranking and Allocation of Funding

Funding under this call is awarded following a rolling call procedure. Applications may be submitted at any time while the call is open. Applications are evaluated at regular intervals, typically every 2 to 3 months, or earlier if the number of submitted applications or budget availability so requires.

Following each evaluation round, eligible applications are ranked in order of merit, and funding is allocated until the available budget under this call is exhausted. In cases of oversubscription, priority is given to higher-ranked applications. Where applications receive identical or comparable evaluation results, tie-break rules promoting underrepresented groups, including women and students from disadvantaged socio-economic backgrounds, will be applied in line with Phortify DEI objectives.

Selection Committees

Applications are evaluated by local selection committees established by the Phortify partner institutions. Committees apply this evaluation framework consistently and impartially. Members must declare any conflicts of interest and ensure appropriate mitigation measures.

Documentation and transparency

Evaluation outcomes and funding decisions are documented by the partner institutions. Awarded grants are communicated to the Phortify Coordinator. Aggregate data will be reported in accordance with the project’s reporting obligations.

Available funding under this call

Type and duration of financial support

Financial support under this call is provided either as a monthly allowance or as a lump sum, depending on the Phortify partner institution.

Monthly allowances are paid for the actual duration of the internship, subject to partner-specific conditions. Lump-sum grants are not linked to a fixed duration and are intended to contribute to the overall costs associated with the internship, such as travel, accommodation, and subsistence.

AFS:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 1.200/month for master students

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 800/month for bachelor students

ICFO:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 600/month for a maximum duration of 6 months

TU/e:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 2.000 - lump sum not linked to duration

WUT:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 2.000 - lump sum not linked to duration

FSU:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 1.500 - lump sum not linked to duration


Financial support may only be used for the activities listed above; no other activities are eligible.
description:
About Phortify

Phortify - Photonics Education Network for Next-Gen Innovation and Digital Skills Excellence for Industry and Society - is dedicated to the Enhancement and Harmonisation of Photonics education and training across Europe. Phortify offers a two-year European Master’s in Photonics Engineering, combining advanced coursework, hands-on laboratory training, and cutting-edge digital skills development, structured mobility windows and industry placements. Students who complete the Phortify track receive an official Phortify Certificate in addition to their Master’s degree. Students can enrol in a Phortify-related master programme at any of the 7 participating universities. In addition, Phortify provides stand-alone modules with harmonised standards for quality assurance and certification, offering high flexibility and mobility for both students and industry professionals. Finally, Phortify organises mentoring programmes for women postdocs and early PIs as well as one-day immersive experience events for prospective students, providing a unique opportunity to explore photonics and its applications.

About the Phortify Funding Framework

Phortify’s Funding Framework aims to widen participation in photonics by supporting students and staff who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM. This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.

description:
About Phortify

Phortify - Photonics Education Network for Next-Gen Innovation and Digital Skills Excellence for Industry and Society - is dedicated to the Enhancement and Harmonisation of Photonics education and training across Europe. Phortify offers a two-year European Master’s in Photonics Engineering, combining advanced coursework, hands-on laboratory training, and cutting-edge digital skills development, structured mobility windows and industry placements. Students who complete the Phortify track receive an official Phortify Certificate in addition to their Master’s degree. Students can enrol in a Phortify-related master programme at any of the 7 participating universities. In addition, Phortify provides stand-alone modules with harmonised standards for quality assurance and certification, offering high flexibility and mobility for both students and industry professionals. Finally, Phortify organises mentoring programmes for women postdocs and early PIs as well as one-day immersive experience events for prospective students, providing a unique opportunity to explore photonics and its applications.

About the Phortify Funding Framework

Phortify’s Funding Framework aims to widen participation in photonics by supporting students and staff who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM. This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.

The framework ensures transparency, equal treatment of applicants, consistency across partner institutions, and alignment with the objectives of the Phortify project, including its Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) principles.

2.   Evaluation Principles

The evaluation process is based on the following principles:

  1. Transparency and traceability of decisions
  2. Equal and fair treatment of all applicants
  3. Merit-based selection
  4. Consideration of DEI objectives in line with EU guidance

3.   Evaluation Process Overview

The evaluation consists of two sequential stages:

  1. Eligibility verification (pass/fail)
  2. Comparative assessment and ranking

4.   Stage 1 – Eligibility Verification

Applications are checked for compliance with all eligibility requirements defined in the call text. Applicants must submit all required supporting documentation, including academic transcripts, a Phortify-specific motivation letter, and a curriculum vitae (CV).

Applications that fail to meet the eligibility requirements or that do not include the required documentation are declared ineligible and are not further evaluated.

5.   Stage 2 – Comparative Assessment

Eligible applications are assessed comparatively using the criteria below. Each criterion is scored independently on a scale from 0 to 5 points.

Evaluation Criteria

  1. Academic Excellence (0/5): Academic performance, relevance of previous studies, and preparedness for the proposed Master's thesis project.
  2. Motivation and Alignment with Phortify Objectives (0/5): Quality, coherence, and relevance of the motivation letter, including alignment with Phortify’s educational and societal objectives.
  3. Overall Applicant Profile (0/5): Skills, experience, background, and potential contribution to the Phortify community, as reflected in the CV.

Maximum total score: 15 points.

Ranking and Allocation of Funding

Funding under this call is awarded following a rolling call procedure. Applications may be submitted at any time while the call is open. Applications are evaluated at regular intervals, typically every 2 to 3 months, or earlier if the number of submitted applications or budget availability so requires.

Following each evaluation round, eligible applications are ranked in order of merit, and funding is allocated until the available budget under this call is exhausted. In cases of oversubscription, priority is given to higher-ranked applications. Where applications receive identical or comparable evaluation results, tie-break rules promoting underrepresented groups, including women and students from disadvantaged socio-economic backgrounds, will be applied in line with Phortify DEI objectives.

Selection Committees

Applications are evaluated by local selection committees established by SMART Photonics, in coordination with the Phortify Consortium. Committees apply this evaluation framework consistently and impartially. Members must declare any conflicts of interest and ensure appropriate mitigation measures.

Documentation and transparency

Evaluation outcomes and funding decisions are documented by the partner institutions. Awarded grants are communicated to the Phortify Coordinator. Aggregate data will be reported in accordance with the project’s reporting obligations.

Available funding under this call

Type and duration of financial support

Under this pilot call, up to two (2) Master's thesis projects may be supported, subject to budget availability and the outcome of the evaluation process.

Financial support under this call is provided in the form of lump-sum grants not linked to duration. Lump-sum amounts are intended to contribute to expenses related to activities carried out within the supported Master’s thesis projects, such as travel, accommodation, and subsistence.

SMART PHOTONICS

Phortify Grants for Master Thesis Projects of €3.150 - lump sum not linked to duration


Financial support may only be used for the activities listed above; no other activities are eligible.
